summary_brief: 2026年5月12日，AI Agent生态从"企业集成叙事"（May 9-11）正式进入"多智能体生产落地深化"阶段。今日最大新特征：ErikBjare/gptme的subagent角色系统与Claude Code Agent View形成开源-商业互补格局，多智能体协作从平台架构讨论具象化为可量产的工程模式；Anthropic多语言SDK（Python/TS/Go）同步落地AWS平台支持，标志着企业采纳叙事经过5天铺垫后正式兑现为可部署选项。同时，今日安全加固从被动CVE修复（May 7-8安全债务链）升格为主动CI/CD门控强制执行，评测体系引入graduated partial-credit scoring标志着eval从定性走向科学量化。28信号/12高影响（43%），活跃仓库44个/965 commits，与May 6-11高位平台完全对齐，属于同一活跃周期的自然深化而非新的转折点。

releases.author: ashwin-ant
releases.summary:
## What's changed

- Improved Agent tool `subagent_type` matching to accept case- and separator-insensitive values (e.g. `"Code Reviewer"` resolves to `code-reviewer`)
- Updated agent color palette
- Fixed `/goal` silently hanging when `disableAllHooks` or `allowManagedHooksOnly` is set — now shows a clear message instead of an indicator that never resolves
- Fixed a regression in settings hot-reload where symlinked settings files caused misattributed change events and spurious `ConfigChange` hooks
- Fixed `claude --bg` failing with "connection dropped mid-request" when the background service was about to idle-exit
- Fixed background service startup failing on machines with enterprise endpoint security by allowing more time
- Fixed remote managed settings not retrying on 401 — now retries once with a force-refreshed token
- Fixed managed `extraKnownMarketplaces` auto-update policy not being persisted to `known_marketplaces.json`
- Fixed `/loop` scheduling redundant wakeups to poll for background tasks that already notify on completion
- Fixed a recurring event-loop stall on Windows when a missing executable (e.g. `gh`) triggered synchronous `where.exe` re-spawns on every check
- Fixed `Read` tool calls failing validation when `offset` is passed as a whitespace-padded or `+`-prefixed string
- Fixed native terminal cursor not staying at the input caret when the terminal loses focus
- Plugins now warn when a default component folder (e.g. `commands/`) is silently ignored because `plugin.json` sets the matching key. Shown in `/doctor`, `claude plugin list`, and `/plugin`.

key_changes: Agent tool subagent_type 匹配逻辑优化，支持大小写和分隔符不敏感匹配（如 "Code Reviewer" 自动解析为 code-reviewer）
修复 /goal 命令在禁用 hooks 时静默挂起的问题，现在会显示明确错误信息
修复设置热重载时符号链接文件导致的变更事件误归属和虚假 ConfigChange 钩子触发
修复后台服务在空闲退出时出现的 "connection dropped mid-request" 错误
修复 Windows 平台缺失可执行文件导致的周期性事件循环阻塞问题
ai_summary.summary_cn: 此版本主要修复了多个影响用户体验的 bug，包括 /goal 命令在特定配置下挂起、后台服务的连接问题、设置热重载的符号链接处理问题，以及 Windows 平台的性能问题。同时改进了 Agent tool 的类型匹配逻辑，使其更加灵活。

releases.author: laipz8200
releases.summary:
## 🚀 What's New in v1.14.1?

v1.14.1 is a patch release focused on security hardening, workflow and knowledge-base stability, deployment cleanup, and continued UI platform migration after v1.14.0.

### 🔐 Security

- **Self-hosted `SECRET_KEY` hardening** — Docker deployments no longer rely on a public default key. When `SECRET_KEY` is left empty, the API generates and persists a runtime key through the configured storage backend, while explicitly configured keys continue to work as before. Thanks @laipz8200 in [#36049](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/36049).
- **Internal metrics endpoint protection** — `/threads` and `/db-pool-stat` are hardened to avoid unauthenticated exposure of internal runtime and database-pool details. Thanks @orbisai0security in [#35665](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35665).
- **Account and tool isolation** — fixed an IDOR issue in `GET /account/avatar` and scoped builtin-tool default-credential cleanup to the current tenant. Thanks @NeatGuyCoding and @GareArc in [#35771](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35771) and [#35887](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35887).
- **Dependency security** — upgraded LiteLLM for CVE-2026-42208 and refreshed several backend dependencies, including `urllib3`, `gunicorn`, `gitpython`, `mako`, Google SDK packages, storage libraries, and OpenTelemetry exporter packages. Thanks @crazywoola in [#35953](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35953), [#35779](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35779), [#35791](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35791), [#35863](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35863), [#35864](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35864), [#35958](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35958), [#36011](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/36011), [#36012](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/36012), [#36013](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/36013), [#36017](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/36017), and [#36050](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/36050).

### 🧩 Workflow, HITL, and app runtime

- **Workflow stability** — restored workflow-version loading through the backend API, fixed online-user polling for large app lists, prevented preview resize observer loops, and avoided schema model collisions in trial workflows. Thanks @hjlarry and @lyzno1 in [#35817](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35817), [#35786](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35786), [#35936](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35936), and [#36061](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/36061).
- **Workflow authoring polish** — fixed variable reference picker behavior for sub-variables, workflow node title overflow, condition operator popovers, workflow checklist semantics, and KB metadata filter field selection. Thanks @iamjoel, @hjlarry, @lyzno1, and @shawny011717 in [#35732](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35732), [#35740](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35740), [#35828](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/35828), [#36006](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/36006), and [#34149](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/34149).
- **Workflow execution correctness** — preserved single-run input variable types, fixed `structured_output_enabled` validation, fixed file-preview URL handling in node output display, and unblocked plugin model selector tools on v1.14.0 workflows. ## Upgrade Guide

### Important notes

- This release includes a new database migration for configurable Explore app categories. Run database migrations as part of the upgrade.
- Docker Compose environment variables are now split into categorized files under `docker/envs/**`. If you maintain a customized `docker-compose.yaml` or `.env`, review the new layout and re-apply local customizations carefully.
- For self-hosted deployments, explicitly configured `SECRET_KEY` values continue to be respected. If `SECRET_KEY` is empty, Dify now generates and persists a runtime key automatically.

### Docker Compose Deployments

1. Back up your customized docker-compose YAML and env files.

   ```bash
   cd docker
   cp docker-compose.yaml docker-compose.yaml.$(date +%s).bak
   cp .env .env.$(date +%s).bak 2>/dev/null || true
   ```

2. Get the latest code from the release branch or tag.

   ```bash
   git fetch --tags
   git checkout 1.14.1
   ```

3. Stop the service. Please execute in the `docker` directory.

   ```bash
   docker compose down
   ```

4. Back up data.

   ```bash
   tar -cvf volumes-$(date +%s).tgz volumes
   ```

5. Review the new `docker/envs/**` env file layout and re-apply any local customizations.

6. Upgrade services.

   ```bash
   docker compose up -d
   ```

### Source Code Deployments

1. Stop the API server, Worker, and Web frontend Server.

2. Get the latest code from the release tag.

   ```bash
   git fetch --tags
   git checkout 1.14.1
   ```

3. Update Python dependencies.

   ```bash
   cd api
   uv sync
   ```

4. Run the migration script.

   ```bash
   uv run flask db upgrade
   ```

5. Restart the API server, Worker, and Web frontend Server.

releases.summary:
## What's changed

- Added agent view (Research Preview): a single list of every Claude Code session — running, blocked on you, or done. Run `claude agents` to get started. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view
- Added `/goal` command: set a completion condition and Claude keeps working across turns until it's met. Works in interactive, `-p`, and Remote Control. Shows live elapsed/turns/tokens as an overlay panel
- Added `/scroll-speed` command to tune mouse wheel scroll speed with a live preview
- Added `claude plugin details <name>` to show a plugin's component inventory and projected per-session token cost
- Added transcript view navigation: `?` for keyboard shortcuts, `{`/`}` to jump between user prompts, `v` to toggle shortcut panel
- Added hook `args: string[]` field (exec form) that spawns the command directly without a shell, so path placeholders never need quoting
- Added hook `continueOnBlock` config option for `PostToolUse` — set to `true` to feed the hook's rejection reason back to Claude and continue the turn
- MCP stdio servers now receive `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` in their environment, matching hooks. Plugin configs can reference `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in commands
- Compaction prompt now asks the model to preserve sensitive user instructions
- `/mcp` Reconnect now picks up `.mcp.json` edits without a restart, and shows the HTTP status and URL when reconnecting fails
- `/context all` per-skill token estimates now account for the model's tokenizer and show rounded values
- `claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace>` now auto-refreshes the marketplace and retries before reporting a plugin as not found
- `/plugin` installed-plugin details now show hook event names and MCP server names cleanly
- `/context` now shows the providing plugin's name for plugin-sourced skills
- Remote MCP server reconnect retry on transient failures is now enabled for all users
- API requests from subagents now carry `x-claude-code-agent-id` / `x-claude-code-parent-agent-id` headers, and `claude_code.llm_request` OTEL spans include `agent_id` / `parent_agent_id` attributes
- Remote Control, `/schedule`, claude.ai MCP connectors, and notification preferences are now disabled when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `apiKeyHelper` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is set, even if a Claude.ai login also exists. Unset the API key to use these features
- Fixed a deadlock where expired credentials and the `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` policy setting blocked `claude auth login`/`logout`/`status` with no way to recover
- Fixed `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` not auto-approving commands with shell expansions like `$VAR` and `$(cmd)`
- Fixed a bug where a hook writing to the terminal could corrupt an on-screen interactive prompt; hooks now run without terminal access
- Fixed unbounded memory growth when an HTTP/SSE MCP server streams non-protocol data — response bodies now capped at 16 MB per SSE frame
- Fixed `Skill(name *)` permission rules — the wildcard form now works as a prefix match, matching `Bash(ls *)` behavior
- Fixed settings hot-reload not detecting edits to symlinked `~/.claude/settings.json`
- Fixed plugin details failing to load when the marketplace key differs from the manifest name
- Fixed `/model` picker "Default" row not reflecting `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`/`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` overrides
- Fixed spurious "stream idle timeout" 5 minutes after a response completed, caused by the watchdog timer not being cleared on stream cancellation
- Fixed silent `exit 1` when 10+ MCP servers are configured and the cache directory is unwritable — the error message now includes the underlying cause
- Fixed a typing cursor blinking on tab names, list pointers, and select rows in dialogs
- Fixed transcript view letter shortcuts not working after mouse click
- Fixed Bash-mode up-arrow history repeating the first entry and clobbering the in-progress draft
- Fixed pasting or dropping multiple images only inserting the last one
- Fixed hyperlinks using unreadable dark navy on dark themes — they now adapt to the active theme
- Fixed model picker showing a redundant "Current model" row for third-party users whose model is set to the `opus` alias
- Fixed legacy Opus picker entry on PAYG 3P providers resolving to the same model as the default entry
- Fixed mouse wheel scrolling speed in Cursor and VS Code 1.92–1.104; the trackpad now scrolls at a steady rate and the mouse wheel keeps ~3 lines per notch
- Fixed scroll behavior in Windows Terminal and VS Code when attached to background sessions
- Fixed MCP resources from disconnected servers lingering in `@server:` autocomplete
- Fixed two-file diff snippets over-reporting the number of truncated lines by one
- Fixed Grep results not relativizing Windows drive-letter paths and count mode reporting wrong totals for single-file paths
- Fixed border-embedded text overflowing on CJK/emoji due to visual cell width miscalculation
- Fixed fuzzy-match highlighting splitting emoji and astral-plane characters mid-pair
- Fixed skill argument names containing regex metacharacters breaking argument substitution
- Fixed ProgressBar rendering a full block for an almost-full fractional cell
- Fixed task polling and `fs.watch` being resurrected when the last subscriber leaves while a fetch is in flight
- Fixed plugin dependency resolution leaving a stale count when the manifest name differs from the source identifier
- Fixed Insights Time-of-Day chart skewing when a session has an unparseable timestamp
- Fixed keybindings using only the cmd/super/win modifier being flagged as unparseable
- Fixed `claude_code.active_time.total` OpenTelemetry metric not being emitted in `--print` mode
- Fixed `claude plugin update` not preserving cross-plugin symlinks inside a marketplace
- [VSCode] Press Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+T to reopen the most recently closed session tab, configurable via `claudeCode.enableReopenClosedSessionShortcut`

key_changes: 新增 Agent View（研究预览）：运行 `claude agents` 查看所有会话的统一列表
新增 `/goal` 命令：设置完成条件后 Claude 跨轮次持续工作，显示实时耗时/轮次/Token 统计
新增 `/scroll-speed` 命令：可调节鼠标滚轮速度并实时预览效果
新增 `claude plugin details <name>`：查看插件组件清单和预估每会话 Token 成本
增强 Hook 系统：支持 exec 形式的 `args` 字段和 `continueOnBlock` 配置选项
ai_summary.summary_cn: v2.1.139 版本带来多项重要新功能，包括全新的 Agent View 代理视图、跨轮次持续工作的 `/goal` 命令、鼠标滚轮速度调节，以及更完善的插件管理和 Hook 扩展能力。MCP 服务器现在支持 `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` 环境变量，Transcript 视图也新增了快捷键导航功能，整体用户体验得到显著提升。

ai_summary.summary_cn: 本版本主要聚焦安全修复和插件安全加固，更新了 Kiota 和 Snappier 包以修复 NU1903 高危漏洞，同时对 CloudDrivePlugin、OpenAPI 和 gRPC 等插件进行了输入验证和路径验证的强化。此外还新增了 ImageContent 在函数结果中的支持，以及向 OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings 添加 ExtraBody 配置选项。

### Minor Changes

-   88fb6c1: Add `vercel connex attach <client>` to attach a Vercel project to a Connex client for one or more environments. Defaults to the current linked project + all environments (`production`, `preview`, `development`). releases.author: yury-s
releases.summary:
## 🌐 HAR recording on Tracing

[tracing.startHar()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-start-har) / [tracing.stopHar()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-stop-har) expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same `content`, `mode` and `urlFilter` options as `recordHar`. The returned [Disposable](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-disposable) makes it easy to scope a recording with `await using`:

```js
await using har = await context.tracing.startHar('trace.har');
const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://playwright.dev');
// HAR is finalized when `har` goes out of scope.
```

## 🪝 Drop API

New [locator.drop()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-drop) simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element. Playwright dispatches `dragenter`, `dragover`, and `drop` with a synthetic [DataTransfer] in the page context — works cross-browser and is great for testing upload zones:

```js
await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  files: { name: 'note.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('hello') },
});

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  data: {
    'text/plain': 'hello world',
    'text/uri-list': 'https://example.com',
  },
});
```

## 🎯 Aria snapshots
- [expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-pageassertions#page-assertions-to-match-aria-snapshot) now works on a [Page](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page), in addition to a [Locator](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator) — equivalent to asserting against `page.locator('body')`.
- New `boxes` option on [locator.ariaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-aria-snapshot) / [page.ariaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-aria-snapshot) appends each element's bounding box as `[box=x,y,width,height]`, useful for AI consumption.

## 🛑 test.abort()

New [test.abort()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-abort) aborts the currently running test from a fixture, hook, or route handler with an optional message. Use it when you have detected an unrecoverable misuse and want to fail the test right away:

```js
test('does not publish to the shared page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/publish', route => {
    test.abort('Tests must not publish to the shared page. Use the `clone` option.');
    return route.abort();
  });
  // ...
});
```

## New APIs

### Browser, Context and Page
- Event [browser.on('context')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browser#browser-event-context) — fired when a new context is created on the browser.
- [BrowserContext](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext) now mirrors lifecycle events from its pages: [browserContext.on('download')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-download), [browserContext.on('frameattached')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-frame-attached), [browserContext.on('framedetached')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-frame-detached), [browserContext.on('framenavigated')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-frame-navigated), [browserContext.on('pageclose')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-page-close), [browserContext.on('pageload')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-page-load).

### Locators and Assertions
- New option `description` in [page.getByRole()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-role) / [locator.getByRole()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-get-by-role) / [frame.getByRole()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-frame#frame-get-by-role) / [frameLocator.getByRole()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-framelocator#frame-locator-get-by-role) for matching the [accessible description](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#dfn-accessible-description).
- New option `pseudo` in [expect(locator).toHaveCSS()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locatorassertions#locator-assertions-to-have-css) reads computed styles from `::before` or `::after`.
- New option `style` in [locator.highlight()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-highlight) applies extra inline CSS to the highlight overlay, plus new [page.hideHighlight()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-hide-highlight) to clear all highlights.

### Network
- [webSocketRoute.protocols()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-websocketroute#web-socket-route-protocols) returns the WebSocket subprotocols requested by the page.
- New option `noDefaults` in [browserType.connectOverCDP()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-connect-over-cdp) disables Playwright's default overrides on the default context (download behavior, focus emulation, media emulation), so attaching to a user's daily-driver browser doesn't disturb its state.

### Errors and Reporting
- New [webError.location()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-weberror#web-error-location) mirrors [consoleMessage.location()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-consolemessage#console-message-location).
- [consoleMessage.location()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-consolemessage#console-message-location) now exposes `line` / `column` properties (`lineNumber` / `columnNumber` are deprecated).
- New [testInfoError.errorContext](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfoerror#test-info-error-error-context) surfaces additional diagnostic context, such as the aria snapshot of the receiver at the time of an `expect(...)` matcher failure.
- [reporter.onError()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-reporter#reporter-on-error) now receives a `workerInfo` argument with details about the worker for fixture teardown errors.

### Test runner
- New `{testFileBaseName}` token in [testProject.snapshotPathTemplate](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testproject#test-project-snapshot-path-template) — file name without extension.
- Test runner now errors when a config tries to override a non-option fixture, and rejects `workers: 0` or negative values.

## 🛠️ Other improvements
- HTML reporter:
  - `npx playwright show-report` accepts `.zip` files directly — no need to unzip first.
  - Steps that contain attachments inside nested children show an indicator on the parent step.
  - The `repeatEachIndex` is shown in the test header when non-zero.
- Trace Viewer adds a pretty-print toggle for JSON / form request and response bodies in the network details panel.

## Breaking Changes ⚠️
- Removed long-deprecated APIs:
  - `Locator.ariaRef()` — use the standard [locator.ariaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-aria-snapshot) pipeline.
  - `handle` option on `BrowserContext.exposeBinding` and `Page.exposeBinding`.
  - `logger` option on `BrowserType.connect` and `BrowserType.connectOverCDP` — use [tracing](https://playwright.dev/docs/trace-viewer) instead.
  - Context options `videosPath` / `videoSize` — use `recordVideo` instead.

## Browser Versions
- Chromium 148.0.7778.96
- Mozilla Firefox 150.0.2
- WebKit 26.4

This version was also tested against the following stable channels:
- Google Chrome 147
- Microsoft Edge 147

key_changes: 新增 tracing.startHar()/stopHar() API，将 HAR 录制功能集成到 Tracing 中，支持 content、mode、urlFilter 等选项
新增 locator.drop() 方法，模拟外部文件或剪贴板数据拖放到元素上，支持 files 和 data 参数
expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot() 现在支持直接对 Page 对象进行断言，等同于 page.locator('body')

issue_insights.summary_brief: 跨仓库 P0 级问题中，rate_limit_event 未被后端识别导致 spec 创建阶段反复失败（影响 139 个仓库），运行时容器启动失败（micromamba 缺失）影响 30+ 仓库，是当前最广泛的共性问题。单仓层面，workflow_runtime 类问题（模型 ID 映射错误、API 认证失败、流式响应中断）占主导，auth_permission 和 session_state 问题次之。

source_issues.title: Hitting rate limits on Claude Max plan and task fails (rate_limit_event)

top_pain_points.topic: Auth re-auth loop during long-running tasks causes repeated task-blocking pauses
top_pain_points.summary: Users experience repeated authentication pauses during task execution even after successfully re-authenticating. The backend writes AUTH_PAUSE on token failure, user resumes, and the task fails auth again shortly after, creating a persistent re-auth loop that blocks task completion.
aliases: AsyncOpenAI api_key empty string v2.34.0 regression
Windows PATH precedence over bundled tools
empty api_key rejection breaking local servers
toolRunner auth header dropped on follow-up calls
top_pain_points.review_reason: P0: count=2 with strong evidence. Issue 1876 is a detailed root-cause analysis with 5 identified technical causes. Issue 1878 is a separate crash-recovery failure. Both are auth-related and block task completion. The re-auth loop is a clear workflow blocker: users cannot complete long-running tasks without repeated intervention. Count=2 meets the high-frequency threshold with corroborating root-cause analysis.

source_issues.title: Auth loop in tasks: repeated re-authentication due to token/env precedence and credential parsing drift
source_issues.evidence: Users hit auth failure -> backend writes AUTH_PAUSE and waits -> user re-authenticates and resumes -> task can fail auth again shortly after, requiring repeated re-auth within the same task. 5 root causes identified: token format mismatch (backend only accepts sk-ant-oat01-* vs frontend accepting sk-ant-*), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR precedence contradicted by forced token injection, task path not using proactive/reactive refresh machinery, credential schema drift (claudeAiOauth vs oauthAccount), and broad auth error classification over-triggering pause state.

source_issues.title: claude-code-review workflow template generates insufficient permissions; action silently swallows write failure
source_issues.evidence: Generated template sets `pull-requests: read` but posting reviews requires write. Action exits 0 on 403 — no feedback loop, green checks, zero review output.

source_issues.title: [BUG] VSCode 2.1.139: acceptEdits / Edit automatically mode still prompts for Edit tool approval (regression persists since v2.1.79)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduces 100% reliably. 60+ versions unfixed despite multiple closed duplicate reports (#37518, #31827, #36348, #43283, #43953). Root cause identified as 1-line guard missing in requestToolPermission. Forces users into bypassPermissions, which has broader blast radius. Breaks autonomous multi-agent workflows relying on acceptEdits semantics.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Permission-mode cycling causes misplaced system-reminder attachments flagged as prompt injection
source_issues.evidence: 244 handleCycleMode events captured in 17.4s during Shift+Tab autorepeat. Session ID provided (e9f537df). HackerOne report #3730798 submitted. Named third parties (anthropic.com, bing.com) are falsely blamed by Claude as serving prompt injection content. False positives train users to dismiss real warnings, degrading security posture. Also linked to a broader trust-laundering chain documented in the HackerOne submission.

source_issues.title: 用户角色只能是user,没有admin用户

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Infinite loading shown on 'Sign Up With Cline' button after cancelling login process
source_issues.evidence: Cancelling login mid-way leaves infinite loading on sign-up button. Button is not clickable after cancellation.

signals.topic: Auth re-auth loop during long-running tasks causes repeated task-blocking pauses
signals.summary: Users experience repeated authentication pauses during task execution even after successfully re-authenticating. The backend writes AUTH_PAUSE on token failure, user resumes, and the task fails auth again shortly after, creating a persistent re-auth loop that blocks task completion.
signals.review_reason: P0: count=2 with strong evidence. Issue 1876 is a detailed root-cause analysis with 5 identified technical causes. Issue 1878 is a separate crash-recovery failure. Both are auth-related and block task completion. The re-auth loop is a clear workflow blocker: users cannot complete long-running tasks without repeated intervention. Count=2 meets the high-frequency threshold with corroborating root-cause analysis.

source_issues.title: Auth loop in tasks: repeated re-authentication due to token/env precedence and credential parsing drift
source_issues.evidence: Users hit auth failure -> backend writes AUTH_PAUSE and waits -> user re-authenticates and resumes -> task can fail auth again shortly after, requiring repeated re-auth within the same task. 5 root causes identified: token format mismatch (backend only accepts sk-ant-oat01-* vs frontend accepting sk-ant-*), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR precedence contradicted by forced token injection, task path not using proactive/reactive refresh machinery, credential schema drift (claudeAiOauth vs oauthAccount), and broad auth error classification over-triggering pause state.

source_issues.title: Terminal resume after crash
source_issues.evidence: 4 terminals with active conversations in agents terminal crashed/restarted. After app re-opened, auto-recovery and auto-resume found 'no conversation found to continue' in each terminal. Verified via direct CLI that no conversation was saved. Conversations lost with no recovery path.

signals.topic: rate_limit_event unhandled by backend causing spec creation phase to fail repeatedly
signals.summary: Backend does not recognize the 'rate_limit_event' message type from the Claude Agent SDK. When users on Claude Max plan trigger a rate limit event, the spec creation phases fail with 'Agent error: Unknown message type: rate_limit_event' and the spec_writing phase fails after 3 attempts.
signals.review_reason: P0: Main spec creation workflow is completely blocked for Claude Max plan users. Multiple repeated phase failures (complexity_assessment, historical_context, spec_writing all fail) with 3 retry attempts each. The 'rate_limit_event' message type from the SDK is not handled, causing task failure. 19 comments indicates community impact. While count=1, the workflow blockage is unambiguous: users literally cannot use the planning/spec creation flow. review_reason explicitly confirms strong user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: Hitting rate limits on Claude Max plan and task fails (rate_limit_event)
source_issues.evidence: User on Claude Max plan experiences 'Agent error: Unknown message type: rate_limit_event' repeatedly during spec creation. All 3 phases of spec creation (complexity_assessment, historical_context, spec_writing) fail with this error. Phase 'spec_writing' failed after 3 attempts. Task cannot complete the planning workflow. 19 comments indicate this is a known issue affecting Max plan users. User confirms traditional claude code CLI works fine without rate limiting errors, confirming this is an SDK version mismatch / unhandled message type in the app.

The agent proceeds with incomplete information, degrading the quality of complexity assessments. Server reports connected (no indication of failure from connectivity perspective), yet tools are inaccessible - a subtle but impactful permission/mount bug. Count=1 but the nature of the failure (key integration broken at a critical phase with incomplete output) warrants P1 rather than P2.

signals.topic: OpenRouter Sonnet behavioral evals silently return 0/32 — eval pipeline regression
signals.summary: OpenRouter-routed Claude Sonnet 4.6 behavioral evals regressed between May 1 and May 12 builds: conversation logs show only system messages and user prompt with no assistant reply, resulting in 0/32 scores and 0.0 run/eval times. The previously-working OpenRouter path now produces generation timestamps but no persisted assistant output, breaking automated behavioral evaluation pipelines that depend on non-zero eval results.
signals.review_reason: This is a functional regression that silently zeroes out behavioral eval results, breaking automated quality measurement pipelines. While count=1 and single-repo, the user impact is severe: the entire eval pipeline returns 0/32 with no error signal, meaning users cannot distinguish a broken run from a genuinely failed evaluation. This blocks the primary feedback loop for automated code quality assessment.

source_issues.title: Fix OpenRouter Sonnet behavioral evals returning empty trajectories and 0/32 results
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction on May 12 commit ea9c9232b: full-suite baseline produced 0/32 results; targeted rerun on merge-conflict-resolution returned baseline 0/3, holdout 0/3, delta 0.0. Every conversation.jsonl missing assistant message. Generation time present (~3-7s) but run/eval time 0.0 and no assistant/tool output persisted. Previously working on May 1 commit da057f30e.

signals.topic: Context expansion causing zero-response failures on models with small effective context windows
signals.summary: Autonomous-mode prompts referencing multiple paths can expand to 280KB+ of inline content via include_paths(), causing zero-response failures (14-15% no_response rate) on grok-4.20 and kimi-k2.6. Users cannot run autonomous/eval scripts without path expansion ballooning context beyond model limits.
signals.review_reason: Direct user impact: autonomous and eval script users experience 14-15% zero-response failure rates on specific models due to context expansion overflow. This forces manual prompt sanitization and breaks transparent automation. Non-blocking because the affected models (grok-4.20, kimi-k2.6) are non-frontier and the failure rate is observable but not universal. A mitigation (env var) is already proposed.

source_issues.title: feat(context): add GPTME_DISABLE_PATH_INCLUDE env var to opt out of include_paths() expansion
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly documents 14-15% no_response rate on grok-4.20 and kimi-k2.6 when a single autonomous prompt references ~6 paths, ballooning to 280KB+. Root cause traced to include_paths() auto-expansion. Workaround of rewriting prompts to avoid triggering expansion was applied but is fragile.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Runtime container fails to start - micromamba not found in runtime:latest
source_issues.evidence: Runtime container fails to start with error: micromamba not found. The default SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE is set to ghcr.io/all-hands-ai/runtime:latest which uses miniforge3 (not micromamba). However the code expects micromamba. Workaround: use ghcr.io/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.42-nikolaik

signals.topic: RemoteConversation completion log writer encoding failure on Windows

signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation on Windows - users who need LLM telemetry data via log_completions cannot use it due to encoding failures. Empty files and log spam indicate silent failures that would be hard to debug, wasting user time and obscuring data.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: RemoteConversation completion log writer uses platform default encoding, causing failures on Windows

Any LLM response containing emoji or non-ASCII characters causes silent failure - empty .json files are created and logs are spammed with warnings. This affects every RemoteConversation user on Windows who enables log_completions for telemetry.

signals.topic: Running tabby causes unstaged git changes to be randomly reverted/dismissed, leading to data loss
signals.summary: When tabby client runs in the background, unstaged git modifications are randomly reverted without any git commands being executed. Users lose unsaved work with no warning. The process monitor shows WriteFile from tabby.exe followed by system writes, suggesting tabby is directly modifying files it should not touch.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear data-integrity / data-loss pain point. Tabby silently overwrites user-modified files that are not yet committed, causing irreversible work loss. The user provides concrete evidence: no git commands ran, yet files were reverted; Windows Process Monitor confirmed WriteFile activity from tabby.exe. This blocks the user's main workflow (coding with uncommitted changes) and creates direct cost (lost work). Count is 1 because only one issue was reported in the dataset, but the severity of silent file content corruption justifies P1.

signals.review_reason: 虽 count=1，但提供了明确的用户影响证据链：启动崩溃 → Gateway 不可用 → Telegram 掉线 → 需手动回滚。配合自动更新失效（issue #1000 同一票），用户被双重锁定，修复 openclaw 版本硬锁定是唯一出路。P1 合理。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID on auto-update + openclaw version lock prevents manual upgrade

signals.topic: AI 聊天执行过程中发送按钮错误回退为默认状态，用户误以为会话已中断
signals.summary: AI 聊天框在模型执行过程中，发送按钮错误地变为默认发送样式（而非停止按钮），用户感受到会话中断。实际会话可能仍在运行（稍后继续返回消息），但 UI 反馈严重误导用户判断。
aliases: AI chat session interruption UI feedback wrong
发送按钮状态错误回退
signals.review_reason: count=1 不足以 P0/P1，但明确是用户体验下降的 UI 状态错误，发送按钮语义错误在长时间等待场景下严重误导用户判断是否需要中断或重试。P2 保留。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: AI聊天框，会话容易中断

signals.topic: /new 或 /reset 命令在长对话后响应严重延迟（1-3秒+），影响会话管理体验
signals.summary: 用户发送 /new 或 /reset 重置会话时，在 20+ 条消息后出现明显卡顿（1-3 秒+），对比原版 OpenClaw 的 100-300ms 即时响应，流畅度从 5 星降为 3 星。
signals.review_reason: count=1，虽有明确性能对比数据（1-3秒 vs 100-300ms），但非主流程阻断（用户仍可使用，只是体验下降），且无其他用户印证。P2 保留，属于非紧急优化项。

source_issues.title: [Performance] /new 命令响应慢，长对话后延迟明显
source_issues.evidence: 20+ 条消息后 /new 响应 1-3 秒+；原版 OpenClaw 对比 100-300ms；延迟随消息数增加；推测根因：Zustand 全量重渲染、无虚拟滚动、DOM 卸载成本

signals.topic: Formatter layer memory leak causing unbounded memory growth and Python OOM crashes during long conversations
signals.summary: TruncatedFormatterBase.format() calls deepcopy(msgs) on every API call, causing Python process memory to grow from ~200MB to 3GB+ over long conversations, eventually leading to OOM crashes. Related null content bugs cause API 400 rejection cascades and TypeError crashes in tool result conversion, creating an infinite crash loop.
signals.review_reason: Multiple severity-1 bugs in the formatter layer (deepcopy memory bomb, null content API rejection, None crash) directly cause: (1) Python OOM crashes blocking long conversations, (2) API 400 rejection cascades creating infinite crash loops. This is a confirmed main-flow blocker with clear memory growth evidence (200MB→3GB+), OOM crashes, and cross-linked cascading failures. Despite count=1, the multi-bug compound severity and confirmed crash loop justify P0.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Formatter memory leak and content:null API rejection cascade
source_issues.evidence: Bug A: deepcopy(msgs) on every API call causes memory to grow from 200MB to 3GB+ over 50+ turns. Bug B: content:null produces 400 Bad Request from DeepSeek API. Bug C: convert_tool_result_to_string crashes on None output (TypeError). Combined with #1426 (empty assistant turns saved on crash), creates infinite crash loop: crash → save empty turn → reload → API rejects null → crash again. Python OOM confirmed.

signals.topic: Documentation website 404 error on /blogs/ page
signals.summary: The agentscope.io/blogs/ URL returns a 404 error, breaking user navigation to blog content.
signals.review_reason: Documentation website link is broken (404), causing user navigation failure. While not a code-level blocker, it is a confirmed user experience issue that prevents users from accessing blog content. Low frequency (count=1) but clear user impact.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 404 error visiting https://agentscope.io/blogs/
source_issues.evidence: URL https://agentscope.io/blogs/ returns 404 error, confirmed via screenshot showing broken page.

signals.topic: Session I/O storage wrappers swallow all DB exceptions and return None, causing silent session data loss
signals.summary: read_session/upsert_session catch all Exceptions and return None instead of re-raising, making DB errors indistinguishable from 'session not found'. Transient failures (timeouts, lock contention) silently discard user session data.
signals.review_reason: Silent session data loss on transient DB failures (timeouts, lock contention). User loses chat history, tool call history, and session_state with no indication of failure. This is a critical session reliability issue.

source_issues.title: Bug: session I/O wrappers in _storage.py swallow DB exceptions and return None, causing silent session data loss
source_issues.evidence: read_session/upsert_session catch all Exception, log warning, return None. Callers treat None as 'no session' or 'save succeeded with no error', silently discarding user data on transient DB failures.

signals.topic: get_function_call strips intentional whitespace from string arguments, breaking file-editing and whitespace-sensitive tools
signals.summary: Function argument .strip() destroys newlines, spaces, and tabs in string arguments. Tools like EditBlock that rely on multi-line replacements fail with misleading 'old_string must not be empty' errors.
signals.review_reason: Breaks core file-editing and whitespace-sensitive tool workflows. Users get misleading error messages ('old_string must not be empty') even when LLM produces valid tool calls with multi-line strings.

source_issues.title: [Bug] get_function_call strips intentional whitespace from string arguments, breaking tools that rely on newlines
source_issues.evidence: agno/utils/functions.py applies .strip() to all string arguments, silently destroying whitespace. File editing tools (e.g., replacing multiple consecutive blank lines) fail with 'old_string must not be empty' even with valid LLM tool calls.

signals.topic: Parallel tool_hooks race in _safe_hook_call_async leaves run_context.messages permanently stale
signals.summary: When parallel tool calls use asyncio.gather, the swap-restore pattern on shared run_context.messages interleaves across sibling coroutines, corrupting message state for all concurrent hooks.
signals.review_reason: Race condition corrupts shared run_context.messages when hooks await during parallel tool execution. Any hook that awaits (DB, logging, LLM) during parallel calls gets stale/corrupted message state.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Parallel tool_hooks race in _safe_hook_call_async leaves run_context.messages permanently stale
source_issues.evidence: _safe_hook_call_async uses swap-restore on run_context.messages, which is unsafe under asyncio.gather. Same run_context shared across parallel FunctionCalls causes message list corruption when any hook awaits (DB call, logging, LLM).

signals.topic: aget_last_run_output returns None when agent.id is auto-generated (not explicitly set)
signals.summary: When agent.id is auto-generated from agent.name during arun(), a new Agent instance with id=None cannot retrieve runs via get_last_run_output because set_id() is not called during retrieval.
signals.review_reason: Run history retrieval always returns None for agents using auto-generated IDs, blocking common session querying patterns. Requires manual workaround of always setting explicit agent.id.

source_issues.title: bug: aget_last_run_output returns None when agent.id is auto-generated during arun()
source_issues.evidence: initialize_agent auto-generates agent.id via set_id(agent). But aget_last_run_output does NOT call set_id(), so new Agent instances with id=None cannot match stored runs. Run history retrieval always returns None.

signals.topic: agentes continue run loses run_context.dependencies, breaking tools that rely on user authentication tokens
signals.summary: After calling agent.continue_run(), run_context.dependencies becomes None. Tools that depend on run_context.dependencies (e.g., for user_token) fail with KeyError, with no provided workaround.
signals.review_reason: User authentication tokens stored in run_context.dependencies become None after continue_run(), causing tools that rely on them to crash with KeyError. No documented workaround exists beyond switching to Redis storage.

source_issues.title: [Bug] agentos: continue run can't use dependencies parameter
source_issues.evidence: run_context.dependencies becomes None after continue_run(), causing KeyError in tools that access dependencies['user_token']. No workaround provided; Redis is suggested as only alternative.

signals.topic: Billing counter incorrectly decreases when switching to free model mid-session
signals.summary: After using a paid model, switching to the free model causes the billing counter to decrease instead of freezing at the last paid amount, indicating a statistical tracking bug.
signals.review_reason: Two identical reports confirm a billing/cost tracking regression. Clear financial impact: users cannot trust the displayed cost, which directly affects billing awareness and potential cost loss.

source_issues.title: Billing issue when switching models mid-session
source_issues.evidence: After using paid model, switching to free model mid-session causes billing figure to decrease instead of remaining unchanged.

source_issues.title: Billing issue when switching models mid-session
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report with identical evidence: billing counter built into OpenCode kept decreasing after switching to free model mid-session.

signals.topic: Native runtime SIGILL crash terminates process on Linux x86_64
signals.summary: OpenCode 1.14.48 intermittently crashes with SIGILL/invalid opcode inside the packaged native ELF binary on Linux, causing complete process termination with no JavaScript stack trace.
signals.review_reason: Critical process termination with hard evidence (dmesg, coredumpctl). The native runtime crashes to kernel level (SIGILL) during normal use, completely blocking the user's session with no graceful error. High severity despite count=1 because it is a crash, not a degraded behavior.

source_issues.title: OpenCode Native Runtime Crash: `SIGILL` / Invalid Opcode
source_issues.evidence: Process terminated by SIGILL in packaged .opencode ELF binary; dmesg shows trap invalid opcode at same instruction pointer on repeated crashes; coredumpctl records crashes for both native binary and Node wrapper.

signals.topic: All image attachments stripped on Linux x86_64 due to Photon WASM loader failure
signals.summary: On Linux x86_64, the Photon WASM image normalization library fails to load silently, causing all image attachments (including valid tiny images) to be stripped with a misleading 'could not be resized below the inline image size limit' message.
signals.review_reason: Complete functional regression for all Linux x86_64 users: every image attachment is stripped regardless of size. Root cause traced to Photon WASM loader returning null, with a misleading error message that hides the real issue. Blocks a core workflow (reading/attaching images) on a major platform.

source_issues.title: All image attachments stripped on Linux x86_64: Photon WASM loader fails silently, masked as 'could not be resized below the inline image size limit'
source_issues.evidence: Photon WASM import resolves to null on Linux x86_64; every image (even 100x100 215-byte PNG) throws PhotonUnavailableError and is omitted; same version works on macOS arm64; error message is misleading and masks the real WASM loading failure.

signals.topic: NumLock number keys and special keys not working in CLI on Windows
signals.summary: NumLock number keys (0-9) and special keys (*, +, -, ., /) produce no output or incorrect output when typing in opencode CLI on Windows 11/PowerShell, despite working correctly in other terminal applications.
signals.review_reason: Direct user input blocking on Windows: NumLock keys are a primary input method for numbers and math operators. When these keys fail, users cannot type numbers or special characters, significantly degrading the CLI experience.

source_issues.title: NumLock number keys and special keys not working in opencode CLI
source_issues.evidence: NumLock number keys and special keys produce no character or incorrect character on Windows 11/PowerShell; same terminal works correctly with other CLI tools (gemini CLI); issue is specific to opencode.

signals.topic: Keyboard input broken for Dvorak layout users on macOS (scancode vs keycode mismatch)
signals.summary: On macOS with Dvorak keyboard layout, opencode reads scancodes instead of keycodes, causing emacs-like keybinds (ctrl+k, ctrl+j) to produce incorrect behavior instead of their intended actions.
signals.review_reason: Dvorak keyboard users on macOS are completely unable to use basic editing keybinds. The root cause (scancode vs keycode) means all emacs-like bindings produce wrong actions, fundamentally breaking the editing workflow for this user group.

source_issues.title: Keybinds messed up on 1.14.48
source_issues.evidence: Dvorak user on macOS Ghostty: opencode reads scancodes from keyboard instead of keycodes; ctrl+k pastes from clipboard instead of cutting to end-of-line; ctrl+j deletes entire input buffer instead of inserting newline.

signals.topic: Prompt caching produces ~40% cache miss rate on back-to-back sequential requests with identical cached system prompts, causing duplicate cache creation billing
signals.summary: Back-to-back `messages.create()` calls with identical cached system prompts miss the cache ~40% of the time and re-bill cache creation tokens. A 2-second sleep eliminates the issue, indicating a server-side cache visibility race. Affects any multi-turn workload without the workaround, resulting in direct double-billing.
aliases: prompt caching cache miss race condition
signals.review_reason: Clear user impact: duplicate billing for cache creation tokens on every back-to-back request pair. Quantified at ~40% miss rate with a 20-trial reproducer. The issue affects all multi-turn workloads that don't apply the 2-second sleep workaround. SDK-agnostic (API-side bug), so likely broader impact.

source_issues.title: Cache misses on second back-to-back `client.messages.create()` (~40% rate)
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows 8/20 trials write identical cache_creation_input_tokens on both R1 and R2 (~40% miss rate). Each redundant write is billed at full cache_creation_input_tokens rate. Sleep 2s between requests eliminates misses. Cost impact: at typical agent prompt sizes (10-100K tokens), duplicate cache creation billing occurs per back-to-back request pair.

signals.topic: Structured output + thinking + tool use interaction produces invalid JSON or skips tool_use blocks in multi-turn conversations, blocking production use
signals.summary: When using `messages.parse` with `thinking` enabled and client-side tools, the model either emits only a thinking block and ends the turn without tool_use blocks, or the final structured output text block contains invalid/malformed JSON. This breaks structured output compliance in production multi-turn agentic workflows.
aliases: structured output thinking tool use conflict
signals.review_reason: Production-blocking: the combination of structured output + thinking + tool use is a core agentic pattern, yet it produces either invalid JSON or skipped tool calls. No reliable workaround exists without sacrificing one of the three features. Impacts any production agent using this common trio.

source_issues.title: Structured output + thinking + tool use: two bugs in multi-turn conversations
source_issues.evidence: Two distinct bugs: (1) model returns only thinking block + empty text with stop_reason='end_turn' instead of tool_use blocks, making messages.parse fail. (2) Final text block contains mixed/invalid JSON or malformed JSON followed by blank lines and valid JSON in the same block. Reporter states this 'makes it difficult to reliably use thinking + tools together with structured JSON output in production.' Multiple interaction states: removing thinking fixes tool calls, removing structured output fixes thinking.

signals.topic: SDK import time is ~209ms due to eager loading of all types, blocking langchain downstream and degrading cold-start performance
signals.summary: Importing the anthropic package takes ~209ms even for a single type import, due to the SDK eagerly loading all types on import. This cascades to downstream packages like langchain_anthropic taking 300ms+ for imports alone. The SDK is described as a 'glorified HTTP client' making this import cost disproportionate.
signals.review_reason: Quantified performance degradation affecting every user of the SDK and all downstream packages. 209ms import time for an HTTP client is disproportionate and measurably blocks langchain integration. Cold-start latency is a known pain point in serverless/containerized deployments.

source_issues.title: Slow imports
source_issues.evidence: python3 -X importtime shows 209ms to import 'import anthropic'. anthropic.lib.tools takes 69ms, anthropic.types takes 116ms. Even 'from anthropic.types.image_block_param import ImageBlockParam' takes 208ms total. langchain_anthropic downstream takes 300ms+ just for imports. Comments confirm this is a known issue affecting all downstream consumers.

signals.topic: Managed Agents API lacks output_config/effort control, forcing users to accept default high-effort and pay 3x cost with 3.3x latency with no workaround
signals.summary: The Managed Agents endpoint `sessions.events.send` rejects `output_config` with HTTP 400, and no surface exists on `agents.create`, `agents.update`, or `sessions.create` to set effort. The platform defaults to 'high' effort for Sonnet 4.6, causing 3x higher costs ($0.31 vs $0.10) and 3.3x slower latency (156s vs 47s) compared to a steered run. Prompt-based steering is a soft L1 lever, not a reliable solution.
signals.review_reason: Clear cost and latency impact with concrete measurements. No API surface exists to control effort on managed agents despite GA availability of the parameter on messages.create. Users following official documentation are blocked from the 'medium effort' recommendation. This is not an edge case — it directly affects the pricing and performance of the managed agents product.

source_issues.title: Managed Agents `sessions.events.send` rejects `output_config` with 400 — no parity with `messages.create` for effort/thinking control
source_issues.evidence: Verified all four API surfaces: agents.create, agents.update, sessions.create, sessions.events.send — none accept output_config/effort. API returns HTTP 400 'Extra inputs are not permitted' on sessions.events.send with extra_body output_config. Cost: $0.31 vs $0.10 per task on Sonnet 4.6 procedural work (3x). Latency: 156s vs 47s (3.3x slower). Platform effort default is opaque — span.model_request_* events do not echo back applied effort.

signals.topic: Claude Code Extension fails to load on UNC/network paths on Windows, displaying cryptic ENOENT error and making the extension unusable in corporate environments
signals.summary: On Windows, opening a VS Code workspace from a UNC network path (e.g., \\server\share\folder) causes the Claude Code extension to fail to load with ENOENT error referencing a non-existent mapped drive. All workarounds (clearing cache, reinstalling, etc.) fail. Users without admin rights to map drives are completely blocked from using the extension on network shares.
aliases: Claude Code extension UNC path failure
Windows network share extension load failure
signals.review_reason: Extension completely fails to load on a common enterprise Windows configuration (UNC network paths). All workarounds fail. Blocking for affected corporate users with no path forward without admin privileges. Clear user impact: the extension is entirely unusable in the affected environment.

source_issues.title: Claude Code Extension fails to load on network paths (UNC paths)
source_issues.evidence: Extension fails to load with ENOENT error 'no such file or directory, lstat G:\\Grupos' when opening folders from UNC paths. All attempted workarounds failed: reinstall, clear workspaceStorage/globalStorage/storage.json, simplify settings.json, reload VS Code. Corporate users without admin rights (cannot map drives) are completely blocked. Extension works on local C:\\ drive. Error persists even after full cache cleanup and reinstall.

signals.topic: toolRunner drops defaultHeaders on follow-up requests, breaking proxy/gateway authentication
signals.summary: The toolRunner helper does not forward defaultHeaders on subsequent API calls during the tool-use loop, only on the first call. This causes authentication failures when using proxies that rely on custom headers (e.g. Cloudflare AI Gateway's cf-aig-authorization).
aliases: toolRunner auth header dropped on follow-up calls
signals.review_reason: 用户主流程阻断：使用 toolRunner + 代理/网关（如 Cloudflare AI Gateway）的用户在工具多轮对话中收到认证失败，直接阻断核心代理计费功能。Cloudflare 官方已确认为 SDK bug，且有完整复现步骤和 workaround。

source_issues.title: `toolRunner` drops `defaultHeaders` on follow-up requests (breaks proxy/gateway setups)
source_issues.evidence: First API call includes defaultHeaders correctly; subsequent calls in tool-use loop drop them, causing 'x-api-key header is required' authentication errors. Cloudflare team confirmed this is an SDK-side bug (cloudflare/ai#408, cloudflare/agents#511).

signals.topic: SDK strips directory paths from filenames in multipart uploads, breaking skills.versions.create()
signals.summary: The SDK's multipart form handling strips directory paths from filenames (stripPath=true by default), causing skills.versions.create() to fail with 'SKILL.md file must be exactly in the top-level folder' because the API receives SKILL.md instead of my-skill/SKILL.md.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：skills.versions.create() 是用户管理 skill 版本的主流程，但 SDK 默认 stripPath=true 导致 API 始终收到错误路径，返回 400 错误。用户被迫使用 workaround（删除重建）代替版本更新，直接阻断版本管理流程。

source_issues.title: SDK strips directory paths from filenames in multipart uploads, breaking skills.versions.create()
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in internal/uploads.js: getName() with stripPath=true splits on / and takes .pop(), stripping directory prefixes. skills.versions.create() fails with 400 API error. Workaround requires deleting and recreating skill instead of using versions.create(). OpenAI Node SDK has the same issue (openai/openai-node#1807).

signals.topic: Streaming responses interrupted mid-transmission without message_stop event on large tool_use JSON
signals.summary: Streaming responses terminate prematurely without sending a message_stop event, specifically when using tool_use with large JSON payloads. The stream consistently ends around 270-280KB with incomplete partial_json data, causing 'Stream ended without message_stop event' parsing errors.
aliases: stream terminates mid-transmission large JSON payload
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：大 JSON payload 的 streaming tool_use 响应被截断，无法完成完整传输。用户在处理文件写入、数据组织等需要大 JSON 结构的 agentic 工作流中反复收到 'Stream ended without message_stop event' 错误，导致核心功能不可用。

source_issues.title: Streaming responses consistently interrupted mid-transmission - connection closes without message_stop event
source_issues.evidence: Stream ends abruptly after ~270-280KB with partial_json='fa', missing content_block_stop, message_delta, and message_stop events. Issue reproduced across multiple maxTokens values. Slowing stream consumption resolves the issue, suggesting backpressure handling failure in SDK's async iterator.

signals.topic: strict:true causes 500 Internal Server Error with complex nested tool schemas
signals.summary: Using strict:true with structured outputs beta and complex nested tool schemas (arrays of objects with required fields) causes API to return 500 Internal Server Error after 17-55 seconds, instead of the documented 400 error or successful response.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：strict:true 结构化输出在复杂嵌套 schema 场景下触发 500 错误，用户无法使用官方推荐的结构化输出模式。错误信息不明确（500 而非文档中的 400），增加调试难度。严重影响企业级 booking 等依赖结构化输出的业务流程。

source_issues.title: [BUG] strict: true causes 500 Internal Server Error with complex nested tool schemas
source_issues.evidence: Complex nested schemas with strict:true (arrays of objects, additionalProperties:false) consistently return 500 error after 17-55s. Same schemas work without strict:true. 500 instead of documented 400 'Schema too complex' makes root cause unclear. Affects booking/enterprise workflows requiring structured output.

signals.topic: Vertex AI: document URL sources rejected with misleading error path
signals.summary: When using @anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk to send a document content block with URL source, the Vertex endpoint rejects it with an incorrect error path: it reports 'image.source.base64.data: URL sources are not supported' when the actual block is type=document with source.type=url.
aliases: vertex document URL source error path wrong
vertex-sdk URL source rejected incorrect error message
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：Vertex AI 场景下文档 URL source 功能不可用（主流程阻断），且错误路径指向 image.source.base64.data 而非 document.source.url，严重干扰调试。文档标注支持但实际不可用，造成用户困惑。

source_issues.title: Vertex AI: document URL sources rejected with incorrect error path
source_issues.evidence: Document content blocks with URL sources are rejected by Vertex endpoint. The error path references image.source.base64.data instead of document.source.url, making debugging difficult. Anthropic docs list URL sources as supported for documents, but Vertex rejects them.

signals.topic: Bundled CLI silently drops TRACEPARENT trace context on 2nd+ query() call in long-running processes, breaking observability
signals.summary: When the bundled Claude Code CLI is invoked multiple times within the same long-running Python process, the W3C TRACEPARENT trace context is silently ignored after the first call. This is triggered by the persistent ~/.claude/ state directory, causing all subsequent CLI spans to emit with fresh trace IDs instead of nesting under the caller's trace. This breaks the entire observability/traces flow described in official docs for server/worker deployment patterns.
aliases: TRACEPARENT trace context dropped on second query call
telemetry tracing broken on repeated SDK calls
CLI ignores TRACEPARENT env after first invocation due to ~/.claude/ state
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: the primary observability/traces flow becomes completely unusable after the first query() call in server deployments. The bug is triggered deterministically by persistent CLI state, has a workaround (unique HOME per call), and breaks the documented Read agent traces workflow. Count=1 but review_reason provides strong evidence: confirmed 100% repro, affects the official hosting deployment pattern, no telemetry past first call without workaround.

source_issues.title: Bundled CLI silently drops inbound TRACEPARENT on 2nd+ query() call when ~/.claude/ has state from a prior run
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed 100% reproduction: first query() call nests spans correctly under TRACEPARENT; second call onwards produces orphaned root spans with fresh trace IDs. Wiping ~/.claude/ between calls restores correct behavior. Affects the dominant deployment shape per official Hosting docs.

signals.topic: SDK crashes with MessageParseError when non-Anthropic-compatible backends emit thinking blocks without signature field
signals.summary: The SDK message parser unconditionally accesses block['signature'] for thinking content blocks. When a non-Anthropic-compatible backend (e.g. gpt-5.4 via Anthropic-compatible API) emits a thinking block without the signature field, the SDK raises MessageParseError and crashes the entire query() call after ~30 seconds of processing, losing all work.
aliases: SDK crashes on thinking block from non-Anthropic backends
KeyError 'signature' in message parser for thinking blocks
signals.review_reason: Real user pain point: the entire query() call crashes after significant processing time, losing all work. This is a main flow failure — the user submits a prompt, waits ~30 seconds, and gets a crash with no result. The root cause is the parser's strict assumption that every thinking block has a signature field, which breaks compatibility with non-Anthropic backends using the Anthropic-compatible API. Count=1 but strong evidence: complete workflow failure, confirmed crash, prior related issues (#339, #473, #786) confirm this is a recurring pattern.

source_issues.title: MessageParseError: missing signature in thinking block with claude-agent-sdk 0.1.79 and Anthropic-compatible backend
source_issues.evidence: SDK crashes with KeyError: 'signature' at message_parser.py:137 when backend emits thinking block without signature. Request runs ~30 seconds then fails before any result is returned. Reproducible with gpt-5.4 via Anthropic-compatible backend. Related to prior issues #339, #473, #786 indicating this is a known recurring incompatibility.

signals.topic: Stderr callback exception silently kills stderr stream delivery for remainder of session
signals.summary: In SubprocessCLITransport._handle_stderr, the user-provided stderr callback is wrapped in a single try/except that catches all exceptions. If the callback raises even once, the entire stderr handling loop terminates silently, dropping all subsequent stderr lines for the rest of the session. Users have no indication that their callback errored.
aliases: stderr callback error terminates stderr stream
stderr callback exception silently drops remaining output
except Exception pass in stderr handler
signals.review_reason: Real bug with clear user impact: a single exception in the user's stderr callback permanently disables stderr delivery for the entire session. This means debugging information and error messages from the CLI are silently lost after the first callback error. The failure is silent with no log or traceback, making it hard to diagnose. P2 because it is non-blocking (the main query still completes) but causes significant debugging/tracing degradation.

source_issues.title: Bug: stderr callback raise silently kills _handle_stderr loop, dropping all subsequent stderr lines
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproduction (5/5): second stderr line dropped when callback raises RuntimeError on first line. Subsequent CLI errors are permanently lost. Silent failure — no log, no traceback. The except Exception: pass swallows all errors without any indication.

signals.topic: TranscriptMirrorBatcher CancelledError pollutes logs during normal SDK shutdown/cancellation
signals.summary: The TranscriptMirrorBatcher's _flush_task uses add_done_callback(lambda t: t.exception()) which raises CancelledError on cancelled tasks in Python 3.8+. This causes asyncio to log Exception in callback with a CancelledError traceback every time an in-flight eager-flush task is cancelled — including during normal event-loop teardown and Query.close() cancellation.
aliases: log noise during SDK shutdown with eager flush
signals.review_reason: Real user pain point: the SDK generates noisy CancelledError tracebacks in production logs and test output during normal shutdown paths. While functionality is unaffected (the drain task handles cancellation correctly via async with self._lock), the log noise is significant for anyone using session_store_flush='eager' and has visible impact on test output and observability. P2 because it does not block main flow but pollutes logs during every normal cancellation.

source_issues.title: Bug: TranscriptMirrorBatcher.enqueue's add_done_callback lambda raises CancelledError when task is cancelled
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed log noise in test teardown output and during normal Query.close() cancellation paths. The bug manifests every time an eager-flush task is cancelled, polluting both test output and production logs. The fix is a one-liner (check t.cancelled() before calling t.exception()).

signals.topic: Linux glibc系统上musl二进制文件被错误选择导致query()执行失败
signals.summary: SDK的二进制选择器在glibc Linux上优先选择musl变体，导致spawn时ENOENT错误，主流程完全阻断。用户即使正确安装了SDK也无法使用query()，且错误信息具有误导性。
aliases: linux binary auto-discovery picks wrong libc variant
musl variant selected on glibc hosts causing ENOENT
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：query()在glibc Linux上完全不可用，spawn失败且错误信息误导用户。count=2，有明确复现步骤和系统性根因分析（resolver先尝试musl且spawn ENOENT不触发fallback），用户被迫手动指定pathToClaudeCodeExecutable作为workaround。

source_issues.title: Binary picker selects musl variant on glibc Linux, causing ENOENT at spawn
source_issues.evidence: query() fails at spawn with misleading 'Native binary not found' error on Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39). The file exists but can't execute due to missing musl loader.

source_issues.title: Linux: musl binary preferred over glibc in v0.2.116 CLI auto-discovery
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on pnpm 10.32.1 with both optional deps installed. require.resolve succeeds for musl but spawn fails with ENOENT. Error message says 'binary not found' when file exists. Workaround requires manually specifying pathToClaudeCodeExecutable.

signals.topic: 使用options.hooks时自定义systemPrompt身份被覆盖为Claude Code
signals.summary: 当传入任何类型的hooks（PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PreCompact/SessionEnd）时，自定义systemPrompt中定义的角色身份被忽略，agent响应为Claude Code。这导致生产多智能体系统必须在可观测性和身份保真度之间做选择。
aliases: systemPrompt ignored when hooks are active
signals.review_reason: 生产环境关键功能受损：多智能体系统中自定义角色身份是核心业务需求。使用hooks实现可观测性是合理实践，但被迫放弃PostToolUse/PreCompact/SessionEnd等hook类型作为代价，体验显著下降。canUseTool作为workaround不能完全覆盖场景，存在功能缺失。

source_issues.title: options.hooks causes agent to ignore custom systemPrompt and identify as "Claude Code"
source_issues.evidence: 生产环境17智能体系统中，hooks被用于可观测性（工具日志、预算守卫、会话生命周期），但任何hooks类型（含空handler）都导致agent忽略systemPrompt中的自定义角色身份。用户被迫迁移到canUseTool workaround，但canUseTool不覆盖PostToolUse/PreCompact/SessionEnd场景。开发人员花费8小时隔离此bug。

signals.topic: 在首条assistant消息之前调用close()导致会话无法恢复
signals.summary: 在收到首条assistant消息之前调用close()，返回的session_id在后续resume时无效，抛出'No conversation found with session ID'错误，导致会话恢复功能在特定场景下完全不可用。
aliases: session non-resumable when close called before first assistant message
signals.review_reason: 会话状态管理缺陷：session resume是SDK核心功能之一，在特定操作顺序下失败会导致开发者需要自行编写workaround检测逻辑。与AbortController行为不一致增加了用户认知负担，虽然最终关闭了issue但bug本身确实存在。

source_issues.title: Bug: Calling `close()` before first assistant message makes session non-resumable
source_issues.evidence: 在brand new sessions中，系统init消息返回的session_id在close()后不可恢复。用户需自行检测是否收到过assistant消息来决定是否恢复。与AbortController行为不一致（AbortController允许在此情况下恢复）。提供了直接复现gist链接。

signals.topic: createSdkMcpServer丢失Zod v4字段级.describe()元数据
signals.summary: 使用Zod v4时，字段级别的.describe()元数据在createSdkMcpServer生成的MCP工具inputSchema中被剥离，工具描述可见但属性描述丢失，导致模型无法看到字段级指导信息。
aliases: Zod v4 describe metadata stripped from MCP tool schemas
property descriptions lost in tools/list schema
signals.review_reason: Zod v4兼容性问题导致工具schema质量下降，字段级指导信息丢失影响模型理解输入结构。虽然不是阻断性问题，但SDK明确声明支持Zod v4而实际存在兼容缺口，属于关键功能不可用（描述信息不可用）。

source_issues.title: createSdkMcpServer drops Zod v4 field .describe() metadata from tool inputSchema
source_issues.evidence: SDK声明peerDependencies支持Zod v4（^4.0.0），但Zod v4的describe()元数据存储在schema实例/metadata registry而非_def.description上，内部转换路径未正确读取导致描述被剥离。影响MCP工具的字段级指导质量。

signals.topic: Action silently exits success with no review when GitHub API permission is insufficient
signals.summary: When the action lacks `pull-requests: write` permission, posting review comments fails with a 403, but the action exits 0 and reports success — leaving required checks permanently green while reviews go nowhere.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：action 成功退出但评审内容从未发布，用户完全不知情，merge gate 形同虚设。影响所有使用模板且未手动修正权限的工作流。

source_issues.title: claude-code-review workflow template generates insufficient permissions; action silently swallows write failure
source_issues.evidence: Generated template sets `pull-requests: read` but posting reviews requires write. Action exits 0 on 403 — no feedback loop, green checks, zero review output.

signals.topic: Anti-loop guard blocks claude[bot]'s own commit, leaving PRs with permanent red required checks
signals.summary: When claude[bot] pushes a commit to address review feedback, the action's own anti-loop guard blocks the downstream run, causing a permanent red required check with no substantive failure in the diff.
aliases: bot-triggered run blocked by actor policy
permanent red check after bot commit
signals.review_reason: 阻断主流程：使用 @claude 处理 review 反馈后，action 自身触发新 run 并被自身策略拒绝，导致 required check 永久 red，用户无法 merge，必须手动 override。

source_issues.title: claude-review blocks itself when triggered by claude[bot]'s own commit — permanent red required check on PRs after @claude addresses review
source_issues.evidence: claude[bot] pushes a commit to address review → pull_request event fires → actor policy refuses run → required check stays red indefinitely. Linked concrete repo: geniuskamo/ghana-realestate-platform PR 1596.

signals.topic: Action intermittently posts CLAUDE.md verbatim instead of structured review, exits success
signals.summary: Intermittently the action posts the repo's CLAUDE.md file as the PR comment instead of the structured review requested by the prompt, and exits success — silently shipping a non-review as a passing check.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能失效：评审本应产出的结构化输出被文件内容替换，且 action 仍然成功退出。Naive 工作流（绿色=已评审）会静默放行未评审的 PR，存在实质质量风险。

source_issues.title: Action posts repo's CLAUDE.md verbatim as comment body instead of structured review (workflow exits success)
source_issues.evidence: Same workflow on two consecutive commits: first produces 676-char structured review, second produces 19,407-char raw CLAUDE.md verbatim. Both conclude success. Model appears to conflate loaded guidance context with content to post.

signals.topic: Branch name validation rejects commas, blocking action on PRs with comma-containing branches
signals.summary: validateBranchName() regex does not allow commas, causing the action to fail before any git operation on PRs where the head branch name contains a comma — even though git and GitHub both accept such names.
aliases: Invalid branch name error for valid git branches
signals.review_reason: 阻断特定工作流：对于使用含逗号分支名的工作流，action 在调用 Claude 前直接失败，且 workaround（重命名分支）不总是可行，影响面覆盖所有分支名含逗号的 PR。

source_issues.title: `validateBranchName()` in `src/github/operations/branch.ts` rejects branch names containing a comma (`,`)
source_issues.evidence: Regex `/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9/_.#+-]*$/` rejects commas. Common branch-naming conventions (derived from titles, place names, external system IDs) produce commas. Action fails before invoking Claude, blocking entire workflow on affected PRs.

signals.topic: Documentation example for parsing execution_file uses wrong field name, silently matches zero events
signals.summary: base-action README example walks execution_log looking for `e.role === 'assistant'`, but SDK events use `e.type` at the top level. The example never matches and silently falls through, causing downstream steps to post nothing without any error.
aliases: e.role vs e.type mismatch in docs
signals.review_reason: 文档级误导导致用户自定义工作流静默失败：按文档实现 execution_file 解析的用户永远取不到 assistant 回复，但得不到任何错误提示，需自行对照源码才能发现根因。

source_issues.title: Docs: base-action README example for parsing execution_file uses stale e.role === 'assistant'; current SDK output has top-level e.type
source_issues.evidence: User follows README example verbatim → core.info('no assistant message found') fires on every successful run. The SDK writes `type: 'assistant'` not `role: 'assistant'`. No error thrown, output silently empty.

signals.topic: Desktop App: Prompt preview overlay blocks diff bar, permission prompts, and workspace controls
signals.summary: On both macOS and Windows, the prompt preview overlay renders as a floating layer covering the diff bar, permission prompts, and workspace buttons with no dismiss mechanism. Users cannot interact with red confirmation prompts or view their session state. Regression from prior versions.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker in the Desktop App. Three separate reports across macOS and Windows all confirm the overlay covers critical UI elements (diff bar, permission prompts, confirmation dialogs, branch selector) with no dismiss mechanism. In Bypass permissions mode, this means destructive actions silently auto-proceed while users cannot see or interact with confirmation prompts. Confirmed regression since 1.6608.x on macOS. count=3 meets the high-frequency threshold.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Desktop App Prompt Preview Overlay covers large portions of the output screen degrading UX and making it hard to read output.
source_issues.evidence: Overlay covers output viewport. No settings to disable. No manual dismiss. Makes it extremely difficult to read text and interact with the program.

source_issues.title: [BUG] [Desktop App Code tab / macOS] Prompt preview overlay covers diff bar and permission prompts
source_issues.evidence: Blue overlay covers diff bar, Create PR button, red confirmation prompt, branch selector, and most of the transcript. Red destructive prompt is completely invisible. In Bypass mode, non-destructive actions auto-proceed while critical prompts silently block progress.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Desktop 1.6608.2 (macOS): user message bubble overlaps previous assistant response in Code view
source_issues.evidence: User bubble renders on top of preceding assistant response — no proper margin/background separation. Visible on every turn when scrolling session history. Regression introduced in 1.6608.x.

signals.topic: Windows: All official MCP plugins using bare `npx` fail with `spawn ENOENT`
signals.summary: Every official plugin shipped with `command: npx` fails to connect on Windows due to a spawn path bug. The LSP fix from #17312 did not extend to the MCP code path. Six official plugins confirmed broken: context7, chrome-devtools, azure, mongodb, desktop-commander, and playwright.
aliases: MCP plugin spawn ENOENT on Windows
npx.cmd spawn failure for MCP servers
signals.review_reason: count=1 but explicitly affects ALL official MCP plugins on Windows (6 confirmed). The workarounds are fragile and get wiped on plugin updates. This is a complete MCP plugin ecosystem failure on Windows, equivalent to the LSP bug that was fixed in v2.1.132. Review reason explicitly provides the strong user impact evidence needed for P0 despite single-instance count.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Windows: plugin-shipped MCP servers using bare `npx` fail with `spawn ENOENT`
source_issues.evidence: Six official plugins confirmed broken with explicit reproducible steps. Workaround requires manually patching plugin manifests in cache directory, which is wiped on plugin updates. The LSP code path was fixed in v2.1.132 but the equivalent MCP spawn path was missed.

signals.topic: VS Code extension: `acceptEdits` permission mode does not work — Edit/Write always prompts (regression since v2.1.79, 60+ versions unfixed)
signals.summary: Selecting 'Edit automatically' mode in the VS Code extension dropdown does not prevent Edit/Write tool approval prompts. Every file edit still triggers the 'Make this edit to [file]?' dialog despite the mode being active. Users are forced into 'bypassPermissions' as the only working option, which is broader than intended.
signals.review_reason: count=1 but has been a confirmed regression for 60+ versions with multiple closed duplicate reports establishing a clear pattern. The issue defeats the purpose of the acceptEdits permission mode entirely, forcing users to use broader bypassPermissions. Strong user impact documented: breaks autonomous workflows. Review reason provides the necessary evidence for P0 despite single count.

source_issues.title: [BUG] VSCode 2.1.139: acceptEdits / Edit automatically mode still prompts for Edit tool approval (regression persists since v2.1.79)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduces 100% reliably. 60+ versions unfixed despite multiple closed duplicate reports (#37518, #31827, #36348, #43283, #43953). Root cause identified as 1-line guard missing in requestToolPermission. Forces users into bypassPermissions, which has broader blast radius. Breaks autonomous multi-agent workflows relying on acceptEdits semantics.

signals.topic: CLI subprocess on Windows silently hangs with zero stdout for 3+ minutes in production automation
signals.summary: Claude CLI invoked as a subprocess from PowerShell automation on Windows hangs intermittently (~<1% frequency but daily impact) with zero stdout for 3+ minutes before either completing or being killed by timeout. No early detection possible. Production automation pipelines with 50-100 invocations/day are affected.
aliases: silent hang zero stdout Windows automation
signals.review_reason: Intermittent CLI hang in production Windows automation. While <1% frequency, the retry overhead and 3+ minute wait per occurrence adds up for high-volume automation pipelines (50-100 invocations/day). The hang is silent with no diagnostic output, making it hard to detect. Mitigation adds complexity and latency. Clear cost/time impact to production workflows.

source_issues.title: Claude CLI subprocess silent-hang: zero stdout for 3+ minutes (intermittent)
source_issues.evidence: Production automation hit the hang on attempt 1 AND 2 back-to-back. Same skill ran cleanly for hundreds of other invocations. User built retry logic with 5-min wall-clock timeout and 3-min silence guard as mitigation. Even with mitigations, each hang costs 4+ minutes of wait time plus backoff. ~1% of 50-100 daily invocations = roughly daily occurrence.
