signals.topic: Permission cycling generates spurious prompt injection flags that misidentify named third parties
signals.summary: Rapid permission-mode cycling (e.g. autorepeat Shift+Tab) produces a backlog of inline system-reminder attachments that the model perceives as inside tool output. The model spontaneously flags these as suspected prompt injection, causing false security warnings and users walking away believing named third-party websites are malicious.
signals.review_reason: False security warnings that misidentify named third parties as malicious are a significant UX harm — users walk away believing real, legitimate websites are compromised. The repeated false positives also train users to ignore real prompt injection warnings, degrading security posture across all future sessions. The issue has clear empirical evidence (244 events in 17.4s) and is linked to a HackerOne security report.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Permission-mode cycling causes misplaced system-reminder attachments flagged as prompt injection
source_issues.evidence: 244 handleCycleMode events captured in 17.4s during Shift+Tab autorepeat. Session ID provided (e9f537df). HackerOne report #3730798 submitted. Named third parties (anthropic.com, bing.com) are falsely blamed by Claude as serving prompt injection content. False positives train users to dismiss real warnings, degrading security posture. Also linked to a broader trust-laundering chain documented in the HackerOne submission.

signals.topic: Summarization cookbook cell 8 crashes with BadRequestError due to deprecated assistant message prefill
signals.summary: Running cell 8 in the capabilities/summarization/guide.ipynb notebook raises a BadRequestError because the assistant message prefill API is no longer supported. Users following the official cookbook hit a blocking failure with a clear API error message indicating the conversation must end with a user message.
aliases: assistant prefill deprecation breaks summarization notebook
signals.review_reason: Confirmed blocking runtime failure. A first-party cookbook notebook fails on a specific cell with a clear BadRequestError triggered by a deprecated API feature (assistant message prefill). Users following the official docs cannot complete the summarization workflow. Labeled as 'bug' by the reporter with full stack trace.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Summarization cookbook fails due to use of assistant message prefill
source_issues.evidence: Cell 8 in capabilities/summarization/guide.ipynb raises BadRequestError: 'This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.' The notebook is completely unusable past cell 8 for any user following the official documentation.

signals.topic: Skills introduction notebook missing prerequisite step to clone GitHub repository
signals.summary: The skills-notebooks-01-skills-introduction notebook instructs users to 'cd /path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' without mentioning that the repository must first be cloned from GitHub. Users following the published docs on platform.claude.com encounter a missing-directory error with no guidance on how to obtain the repository.
aliases: missing git clone prerequisite in skills notebook
signals.review_reason: Confirmed UX/blocking issue. The prerequisite section of an official skills introduction notebook omits the critical first step of cloning the GitHub repository, causing new users to hit a missing-directory error immediately. Labeled as 'bug' by the reporter with step-by-step reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: [BUG] intro to skills should point at github repo as install prereq
source_issues.evidence: Users visiting the official platform.claude.com/cookbook page for skills-notebooks-01-skills-introduction find the first instruction 'cd /path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' with no indication that the directory must be cloned from GitHub first. The reporter explicitly describes frustration trying to follow instructions.

signals.topic: Plugins accepted and marked Published on claude.ai/settings/plugins/submissions do not appear in the marketplace
signals.summary: Plugin publishers receive 'Published' status confirmation but the plugin never appears in the marketplace directory or this repository — blocking plugin discovery for all users.
aliases: plugin not appearing in marketplace after publishing
signals.review_reason: Four separate plugins (Meta VR, Mapbox, sindri, and a fourth from #1822's body referencing a fourth plugin) are confirmed accepted and marked 'Published' yet never appear in the marketplace. This is a clear publishing pipeline bug — the 'Published' status is a false signal, and plugins are not being propagated to the repository or marketplace directory. Plugin publishers' work is effectively invisible to all users. The count=4 is the exact number of distinct issues with this exact pattern, not an estimate.

source_issues.title: Meta VR plugin not listed after marked as published
source_issues.evidence: Meta VR plugin submitted Apr 30, 2026, status flipped to 'Published' two days before this issue. Plugin does not appear in this repository or marketplace directory. Publisher offered to draft a PR adding it to marketplace.json.

source_issues.title: Plugin Not Listed After Acceptance (Mapbox)
source_issues.evidence: Mapbox plugin submitted following official guidelines, acceptance confirmation received, status marked 'Published' in submission page. Plugin does not appear in repository or marketplace after acceptance.

source_issues.title: Plugin marked as Published on plugins/submissions but not available in marketplace directory
source_issues.evidence: Sindri plugin submitted via claude.ai/settings/plugins/submit, marked 'Published' in submission UI, but not visible in official marketplace directory. Publisher asked: 'Is there a step I am missing?'

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: orphaned bun server.ts processes cause CPU drain and message delivery failure
signals.summary: Telegram MCP server processes survive parent exit, enter busy loops at 100% CPU ignoring SIGTERM, silently killing the poller — causing inbound Telegram messages to stop being delivered without any user-visible error.
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues confirm the same root cause: Telegram plugin MCP server processes become orphaned zombies that cannot be cleanly terminated, causing 100% CPU drain (battery/compute resource loss) and silent message delivery failure. All three are open, recent (2026-05-09 to 2026-05-11), with concrete evidence: process tables showing zombie PIDs, system reminders showing MCP disconnects, and server.log evidence of polling churn. The message delivery failure is a main-flow breakage — users' inbound Telegram messages silently stop reaching Claude Code with no visible error.

source_issues.title: telegram plugin v0.0.6: orphaned bun server.ts processes peg CPU 100%, ignore SIGTERM, accumulate indefinitely
source_issues.evidence: Orphaned bun server.ts processes running at 99.9% CPU for 14+ days, PPID=1 (launchd), ignoring SIGTERM — only SIGKILL works. Combined ~200% CPU draw, ~30-40W on Apple Silicon, hot chassis, battery drain.

source_issues.title: telegram plugin: orphan watchdog false-positive kills MCP on Windows during idle
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, process.stdin.destroyed/readableEnded transiently flips during idle, triggering orphan watchdog shutdown with no debounce — MCP child dies, Telegram tools vanish mid-session, no auto-respawn. System reminder: 'deferred tools are no longer available (their MCP server disconnected)'.

source_issues.title: telegram: stuck event loop in old bun server.ts survives SIGTERM, holds Telegram polling slot, breaks new sessions
source_issues.evidence: Stuck bun process (PID 884, PPID=1) ran 31+ hours at 99.3% CPU — all three protection layers (SIGTERM handler, stale-poller killer, orphan watchdog) require JS event loop, which is blocked. Two pollers on same token → 409 Conflict, MCP disconnects, reply tool returns 'sent' but messages never reach user.

signals.topic: Telegram channel poller silently dies when another session runs health check (claude mcp list)
signals.summary: Running claude mcp list or /mcp from any session spawns a fresh bun server.ts, sends SIGTERM to the existing long-running poller, exits, leaving the original session with no inbound polling — messages silently stop without error.
aliases: telegram poller dies on mcp list
signals.review_reason: Confirmed reproduction with clear evidence chain: server.log shows polling churn pattern, pgrep confirms zero bun processes while session is alive, and claude mcp list reports 'Connected' (false positive) masking the broken state. This is a silent main-flow failure — inbound Telegram messages stop reaching Claude Code with no visible error, only detectable via server.log inspection. Affects any user with multiple editor surfaces or who runs health checks.

source_issues.title: Telegram channel poller silently dies after claude mcp list / /mcp health check from another session
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed repro: start long-running session A with Telegram channel, run 'claude mcp list' from another terminal, new inbound Telegram DMs are NOT delivered to session A. server.log shows 'replacing stale poller' followed by 'shutting down' with no following 'polling' line. claude mcp list reports 'Connected' because the health check itself transiently spawns a poller — masking the broken state. pgrep shows zero bun processes while session A's claude is still alive.

signals.topic: servicenow-sdk plugin install fails due to marketplace.json pinning wrong git branch ref
signals.summary: The servicenow-sdk marketplace entry specifies ref='main' but the upstream repo only has 'master' branch — install command fails at clone step with 'fatal: Remote branch main not found'.
signals.review_reason: Exact, verifiable root cause with command output evidence: git ls-remote confirms the repo has no 'main' branch. The error is a complete install failure — users who run /plugin install servicenow-sdk@claude-plugins-official get a clone error with no recovery path. The sha in marketplace.json is already pinned to master HEAD, so the fix is trivial (change ref to 'master') but the bug means the plugin is currently non-installable for all users.

source_issues.title: servicenow-sdk plugin: marketplace pins ref 'main' but repo only has 'master'
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed via git ls-remote: ServiceNow/sdk.git has only 'master' branch (plus docs-gh-pages, gh-pages, playground). marketplace.json entry has 'ref': 'main' and 'sha': <master HEAD>. Full error: 'Failed to clone repository for git-subdir source: Cloning into ...temp_subdir_*.clone... fatal: Remote branch main not found in upstream origin'. Plugin is completely non-installable.

signals.topic: superpowers:brainstorming writes runtime state files into project git working tree, breaking CI/CD
signals.summary: The brainstorming skill writes server.pid, server.log, server-info into <PROJECT_DIR>/.superpowers/<session>/state/ — picked up by git status as untracked directory, causing pre-commit hooks, CI preflight checks, and dispatch systems to fail.
aliases: superpowers brainstorming state in working tree
signals.review_reason: Concrete real-world impact: a multi-host CI dispatch system was blocked when the brainstorming skill wrote .superpowers/ into the working tree, causing a preflight dirty-repo check to fail. This breaks automated code review and any CI pipeline that gates on git status. The root cause is architectural — runtime state files (PID, log, info) are written into the project directory when --project-dir is set, and these are pure runtime concerns with no business in version control.

source_issues.title: superpowers:brainstorming writes runtime state into project working tree (.superpowers/<pid>/state/)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed reproduction: after running brainstorming skill, 'git status --porcelain' shows '?? .superpowers/'. Real-world impact: a multi-host dispatch system rejected a dispatched reviewer agent with error 'dirty_repo: base repo has uncommitted changes: ?? .superpowers/' — blocking automated code review workflows. The issue also reproduces on versions 5.1.0, 5.0.7, and 4.3.1.

signals.topic: setup.sh script fails on Windows due to incorrect venv activation path (.venv/bin/activate vs .venv/Scripts/activate)
signals.summary: Windows users cannot run `setup.sh` because the script hardcodes `.venv/bin/activate`, which only works on Linux/macOS. Windows requires `.venv/Scripts/activate`. This blocks the entire onboarding/setup flow for Windows users.
aliases: setup script cross-platform venv activation failure
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: the setup script fails outright on Windows, completely blocking the onboarding/main flow. The issue provides explicit error output (`.venv/bin/activate: No such file or directory`), step-by-step reproduction steps, and maintainer acknowledgment. While count=1 and single-repo scope prevents P0, the blocking nature of a broken setup script justifies P1.

source_issues.title: Inconsistent Virtual Environment Activation Path for Windows in `setup.sh` Script
source_issues.evidence: Script explicitly fails with 'No such file or directory' when Windows user runs `./setup.sh`; reproducible with exact error message `.venv/bin/activate: No such file or directory` on line 18; confirmed by 2 comments and active engagement from maintainers (recent comment 3 days ago).

signals.topic: xlsx recalc.py crashes on Windows due to unguarded socket.AF_UNIX attribute access
signals.summary: On Windows Python builds lacking AF_UNIX support, `_needs_shim()` raises an uncaught AttributeError that crashes the entire recalc.py script before any LibreOffice work begins. The exception handler only catches OSError, not AttributeError. Users must bypass the skill's macro path and invoke LibreOffice directly as a workaround.
aliases: AF_UNIX AttributeError blocks xlsx recalc on Windows
signals.review_reason: Main-flow crash that blocks the xlsx skill's core functionality on Windows. The AttributeError is uncaught, causing complete script failure on every run for affected Windows Python builds. Confirmed 100% failure rate with a full stack trace. Users must manually invoke LibreOffice CLI as workaround, meaning the skill is unusable for its intended purpose on Windows.

source_issues.title: xlsx recalc.py crashes on Windows: unguarded socket.AF_UNIX access
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace showing AttributeError: module 'socket' has no attribute 'AF_UNIX' at the first line of _needs_shim(), preventing any xlsx recalculation. Reproduction confirmed on Windows 11 with Python 3.14.4 uv-managed install. Workaround requires manually invoking soffice CLI, bypassing the skill.

signals.topic: run_eval.py has 0% skill/command trigger rate in claude -p mode, breaking evaluation framework
signals.summary: The evaluation framework's skill trigger mechanism fails 100% of the time. When using `claude -p`, no query ever triggers skills placed in `.claude/commands/`, including explicit requests like 'run /lucas:memory-layer please'. This makes the entire run_eval.py framework unusable — every should-trigger query scores 0/3, affecting all 8 tested skills across 144 queries.
signals.review_reason: Complete workflow failure that makes the skill evaluation framework unusable. Every single query fails to trigger skills, including explicit invocation requests. Affects all skills tested. This blocks the entire eval/benchmarking pipeline for skill authors — a core use case of the skills repository.

source_issues.title: run_eval.py: claude -p never triggers skills/commands (0% trigger rate across all queries)
source_issues.evidence: Tested with 8 skills and 144 queries; every should-trigger query scored 0/3 including an explicit 'run /lucas:memory-layer please'. Confirmed 0% trigger rate across all eval sets. 8 comments from community confirming similar experiences.

signals.topic: docx skill's node -e inline execution corrupts CJK/non-ASCII content, producing garbled output
signals.summary: When generating .docx files with Chinese, Japanese, or Korean text, the model defaults to `node -e` inline execution which passes the script through the shell, mangling multi-byte UTF-8 sequences. Characters are corrupted before Node sees them, producing garbled or ?-substituted CJK in the output. The model eventually self-corrects by switching to file-based execution, but only after extra token rounds and wasted cost.
aliases: CJK content mangled in docx generation
shell processing corrupts multi-byte UTF-8 in docx skill
signals.review_reason: Produces incorrect output (garbled CJK characters) that requires multiple extra token rounds to recover from. This is a repeated, predictable failure mode for any user generating docx files with non-ASCII content. It causes both output quality degradation and measurable cost waste through unnecessary re-generation rounds.

source_issues.title: node -e inline execution tends to corrupt CJK / non-ASCII content
source_issues.evidence: Detailed reproduction showing shell mangles multi-byte UTF-8 before Node sees it, resulting in garbled/?-substituted CJK characters in output .docx file. Model self-corrects after extra token rounds, but output is already corrupted. Also notes CJK fonts (Arial has no CJK glyphs) as secondary issue.

signals.topic: MCP returns excess uncompressed data causing context congestion with large database results
signals.summary: When Claude Code is accessed through MCP, large database query results are returned without compression, causing context congestion. This degrades the main workflow by filling context with raw data that should be filtered or compressed at the source.
aliases: MCP data volume causes context overflow
database MCP returns unfiltered large result sets
signals.review_reason: Causes measurable workflow degradation: context congestion from unfiltered large data returns blocks or slows the main workflow. While the issue is brief, it describes a concrete failure scenario (large DB query results through MCP causing context overflow) that aligns with known MCP integration pain points.

source_issues.title: MCP returns excess data
source_issues.evidence: User reports that claudecode obtained through MCP does not compress returned data, and large database MCP results cause context congestion. 2 comments discussing the issue.

signals.topic: known_location() returns Iowa endpoint for all Gemini models — Gemini 3.x completely broken on GCP Vertex AI
signals.summary: known_location() hardcodes Iowa (us-central1) for all Gemini variants, but Gemini 3.x only works on global endpoint. API returns 404, model silently produces zero tokens.
signals.review_reason: 2 independent reports confirm same root cause. Main Gemini workflow silently broken — zero tokens generated, no error surfaced, only 404 on API. Confirmed with direct API calls showing endpoint mismatch.

source_issues.title: Regression: known_location() returns Iowa for all Gemini models, breaking Gemini 3.x (global-endpoint only)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed API 404 on us-central1 vs 200 on global for gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview. Session created, model set, but zero tokens ever generated — silent failure.

source_issues.title: Regression: known_location() returns Iowa for all Gemini models, breaking Gemini 3.x (global-endpoint only)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #9141. Closed as resolved — same root cause: Self::Gemini(_) => GcpLocation::Iowa introduced in PR #6393.

signals.topic: Memory leak in Docker when MCP tool returns large responses (~3M chars) — process killed
signals.summary: Large MCP tool responses (3M+ chars) cause memory to spike and never be released inside Docker containers. Process is killed. Works correctly on native macOS/Windows.
aliases: Docker memory leak MCP large response
MCP tool large response memory exhaustion
signals.review_reason: Process killed due to unbounded memory growth after large MCP tool response — explicit OOM kill with docker stats evidence. Blocks Docker deployment users. High impact per incident.

source_issues.title: Severe memory leak in Docker container when MCP tool returns very large responses (~3 million characters)
source_issues.evidence: Memory spikes sharply on ~3M char MCP response, never drops after tool call finishes, repeated calls grow beyond 10GB, process killed. Only occurs inside Docker (native macOS/Windows work correctly).

signals.topic: Many concurrent tool calls cause memory spike and process kill — system becomes unresponsive
signals.summary: Rapid burst of concurrent tool calls (edit + 100+ shell calls within milliseconds) causes memory to peak, system becomes unresponsive, goose process killed.
aliases: Concurrent tool calls memory spike process kill
signals.review_reason: Process killed with logs proving rapid burst of concurrent tool calls (~100+ in <1s). Distinct from Docker memory leak issue (#9153) — occurs in CLI on bare metal. Demonstrates unbounded parallel execution problem.

source_issues.title: Many concurrent tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Logs show 100+ tool calls started within ~1 second. Memory peaked, system became unresponsive, goose process killed. Provider: gemma-4 on CLI (Red Hat Linux).

signals.topic: Ollama driver sends requests to wrong endpoint /v1/chat/completions — causes provider-specific panics
signals.summary: Ollama provider driver uses OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint instead of Ollama's /api/chat or /api/generate, resulting in panics for Ollama type providers.
signals.review_reason: Ollama workflow completely broken — driver hits wrong API endpoint causing provider panics. User cannot complete basic chat session with Ollama provider.

source_issues.title: Ollama driver using /v1/chat/completions instead of /api/chat or /api/generate
source_issues.evidence: Ollama provider sends requests to <BASEURL>/v1/chat/completions instead of <BASEURL>/api/chat. Provider panics. User reproduced by selecting Ollama model — goose starts test by hitting wrong endpoint and gets provider-specific error.

signals.topic: stdio extension timeout config.yaml value ignored — sessions always use 30s hardcoded default
signals.summary: Configuring a custom timeout for stdio extensions in config.yaml has no effect. Every session (200+ verified) snapshots the hardcoded 30s default instead of the configured value.
signals.review_reason: Config value silently ignored across 200+ verified sessions. Users who need longer extension timeouts (e.g., for slow MCP servers) cannot configure it, causing extensions to time out unexpectedly.

source_issues.title: stdio extension timeout in config.yaml is ignored -- session snapshot always persists 30s default
source_issues.evidence: Custom timeout (300s) configured in config.yaml is ignored. Verified across 200+ sessions on v1.33.1 — not a single session recorded the configured value. Extension data always persists hardcoded 30s default.

signals.topic: Agent cache 无法记录和回放自定义工具调用，导致关键自动化流程失效
signals.summary: 当使用 agent 缓存（cacheDir）配合自定义工具时，自定义工具的执行不会被记录到缓存中，回放时也被跳过。这导致依赖自定义工具进行表单填充等关键操作（如登录凭证填写）的自动化流程在回放时失败。
signals.review_reason: 自定义工具缓存失效导致关键自动化流程（依赖自定义工具填写登录表单）在回放时失败，属于主流程阻断性问题。用户提供了详细的源码根因分析，issue 持续活跃（2026-05-11 有最新评论），确认了真实用户影响。count=1 不足以 P0，但 P1 合理。

source_issues.title: Agent cache does not record or replay custom tool calls
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 agent 缓存模式下使用自定义工具进行表单填充（登录凭证），回放时自定义工具被跳过导致登录失败。源码层面确认 v3CuaAgentHandler.ts 的 custom_tool case 未调用 recordAgentReplayStep()，且 AgentCache.ts 的 executeAgentReplayStep 未处理 custom_tool 类型。

signals.topic: Stagehand v3 存储状态持久化失效（userDataDir 不生效、storageState() 方法缺失）
signals.summary: Stagehand v3 中 userDataDir 和 preserveUserDataDir 选项无法持久化浏览器数据（cookies、localStorage），且 storageState() 方法不可用，导致认证状态无法在测试运行之间保持，测试必须每次重新认证。
signals.review_reason: 这是从 Stagehand v2 到 v3 的重大功能性退化（breaking regression）：存储状态持久化是测试自动化的核心需求，userDataDir 完全不工作和 storageState() 方法缺失导致关键功能不可用。用户影响明确（认证无法持久化，每次需重新认证），issue 持续活跃（2026-05-09 有最新评论），提供了完整的问题复现和 workaround。count=1 不足以 P0，但 P1 合理。

source_issues.title: Storage state persistence broken in Stagehand v3 - userDataDir doesn't work, storageState() method missing
source_issues.evidence: userDataDir 目录从未被创建，storageState() 方法在 stagehand.context 和 page.context() 上均不可用。Issue 详细分析了根因：v3 移除了 Playwright 依赖但未重新实现相关 API。用户需要手动提取 cookies 和 localStorage 作为 workaround，但无法处理 HttpOnly cookies。影响标注为 High：认证状态无法在测试运行间持久化，每次运行都需要重新认证。

signals.topic: Login failure with 429 rate limit error after service restart
signals.summary: After restarting the service, users are unable to login and receive continuous HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) errors, completely blocking access to the system.
signals.review_reason: Service becomes inaccessible after restart due to rate limiting (429). This blocks the main flow entirely - users cannot login to use the system. High impact despite single occurrence.

source_issues.title: 最新的main，重启服务后无法登录一直报429
source_issues.evidence: User reports being unable to login after restarting service, getting continuous 429 (Too Many Requests) errors. Main flow completely blocked - user cannot access the system after a restart.

signals.topic: Permission denied error prevents Docker sandbox startup
signals.summary: Users cannot start the Docker sandbox due to a 'Permission denied' error on the docker.sh startup script, blocking initial setup and deployment.
signals.review_reason: Users cannot start the Docker sandbox at all due to permission issue on startup script. Blocks the main flow of using the application in containerized mode.

source_issues.title: sudo make docker-start make: ./scripts/docker.sh: Permission denied make: *** [Makefile:181: docker-start] Error 127
source_issues.evidence: User cannot start Docker sandbox due to permission denied error on docker.sh script. Blocks initial setup and deployment.

signals.topic: Uploaded docx file disappears from conversation window during Q&A
signals.summary: After uploading a docx document for Q&A, the file disappears from the conversation window, preventing the document Q&A workflow which is a core feature.
signals.review_reason: Uploaded document vanishes from conversation UI, preventing the document Q&A workflow. This is a main flow blocking issue for a key use case.

source_issues.title: 上传docx文档问答，对话窗口文件会消失
source_issues.evidence: User uploads a docx file for Q&A, but the file disappears from the conversation window. This blocks the document Q&A use case which is a core feature.

signals.topic: New users can only be assigned 'user' role with no path to admin access
signals.summary: After initial registration, all users are locked to 'user' role with no mechanism to gain admin privileges, making many admin features inaccessible.
signals.review_reason: New users are locked to 'user' role with no path to admin access, preventing use of admin features. This is significant UX degradation and key feature unavailability.

source_issues.title: 用户角色只能是user,没有admin用户
source_issues.evidence: After initial installation and registration, users can only be assigned 'user' role, not 'admin'. Many features are inaccessible without admin role.

signals.topic: Docker sandbox MCP filesystem server intermittent 'Access denied - path outside allowed directories' errors
signals.summary: Docker sandbox MCP filesystem server intermittently returns path access denial errors, requiring container restart to recover, disrupting active conversations.
signals.review_reason: Intermittent MCP path access failures disrupt active conversations and require container restart to recover. This is significant UX degradation for sandbox tool usage.

source_issues.title: docker sandbox模式的MCP服务偶尔会出现：Access denied - path outside allowed directories
source_issues.evidence: Docker sandbox MCP filesystem server intermittently returns 'Access denied - path outside allowed directories' error. Requires container restart to recover. Affects tool usage during active work.

signals.topic: SDK migration auth/UI regressions: login cancellation leaves infinite loading, staging login shows unauthorized error, account details missing, browser settings not visible
signals.summary: Multiple auth and settings UI issues introduced during SDK migration: (1) cancelling login leaves infinite loading on the sign-up button, (2) staging environment shows unauthorized error immediately after login, (3) Account tab missing user name, email, and environment selector after upgrade, (4) Browser settings panel not visible. All four block the settings/auth workflow.
signals.review_reason: Four related auth/UI regressions from SDK migration, all confirmed by QA-labeled issues. Combined count=4, affecting login, account management, and settings access. The staging unauthorized error directly blocks task execution after login.

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Infinite loading shown on 'Sign Up With Cline' button after cancelling login process
source_issues.evidence: Cancelling login mid-way leaves infinite loading on sign-up button. Button is not clickable after cancellation.

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Unauthorized error shown after login when executing tasks in Cline in staging environment
source_issues.evidence: After signing up in staging environment, tasks fail with 'Unauthorized: Please make sure you're using the latest version of Cline' error.

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Account tab details missing after upgrading to latest build (Name, Email, Environment option not displayed)
source_issues.evidence: Account tab shows no user name, no email, and no environment selector after upgrading. Settings panel also missing browser configuration options.

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Browser settings option not visible in Cline Settings
source_issues.evidence: Browser settings panel not visible in Cline settings after SDK migration upgrade.

signals.topic: Cline silently auto-compacts context even when autocompacting setting is disabled, causing agent to forget prior work and task corruption
signals.summary: Despite having autocompacting disabled, Cline silently reduces context mid-task when file reads fill the context window. The context bar visibly shrinks without any user notification, causing the agent to redo completed work, forget user instructions, and forget important conversation state. This is a silent data-loss bug with no user-facing warning.
signals.review_reason: This is a user-visible workflow-blocking bug: the context silently shrinks and the agent loses critical state mid-task, forcing rework. The user's task progress is silently destroyed with no warning. While count=1, the severity is high as it directly corrupts the ongoing work session.

source_issues.title: Cline auto compacts context silently even with autocompacting setting disabled
source_issues.evidence: Context usage bar visibly shrinks from ~90k to ~60k with no notification. Agent redoes completed tasks, forgets user instructions and conversation state. No indication of compaction is shown.

signals.topic: Agent gets permanently stuck in Pending state after command failure, only recoverable via VS Code restart
signals.summary: When a command execution fails (e.g. command word truncation), Cline marks it as 'Skipped' but the agent then enters a permanent 'Pending' state that cannot be cancelled. The user cannot proceed or recover without fully quitting and reopening VS Code.
aliases: stuck Pending state after failed command
signals.review_reason: This is a main workflow blocker: the agent becomes permanently unrecoverable after any command failure, forcing a full IDE restart. This directly prevents task completion.

source_issues.title: Agent gets permanently stuck in Pending state after failed command execution, requires VS Code restart
source_issues.evidence: Failed command causes agent to enter permanent 'Pending' state. Cancel button does not resolve it. Full VS Code restart is the only recovery path.

signals.topic: Streaming response hangs indefinitely on TCP half-open connections with no timeout or retry mechanism
signals.summary: StreamChunkCoordinator.await on network half-open states never times out. When the network connection becomes half-open mid-stream, the UI stays frozen in 'streaming' state forever with no error surfaced and no retry triggered. The only recovery is manually clicking Cancel, which aborts the entire task.
aliases: indefinite streaming hang on network issue
signals.review_reason: This is a main workflow blocker: the streaming state can hang indefinitely on any network instability, leaving the user with a frozen UI and no automated recovery path. The task cannot proceed and manual intervention is required.

source_issues.title: Streaming response hangs indefinitely on TCP half-open connections
source_issues.evidence: StreamChunkCoordinator.startPump() awaits indefinitely on half-open TCP connections. No timeout fires, no retry is attempted. The only way out is Cancel which aborts the entire task instead of retrying.

signals.topic: Settings panel inaccessible without account — gear icon non-functional until user signs up, blocking local provider setup
signals.summary: The settings gear icon does nothing when Cline is used without an account. Users who want to use local providers like Ollama cannot access settings until they sign up for an account, making local-only usage impossible.
signals.review_reason: This is a functional blocker for local-only users: the settings UI is completely inaccessible without an account, preventing configuration of local providers. This is a key workflow block for users who don't want cloud authentication.

source_issues.title: Settings panel does not work without an account
source_issues.evidence: Gear icon does nothing without an account. User had to go through sign-up before the settings pane started working. Local Ollama users cannot configure the extension.

signals.topic: Multiple documentation gaps block feature discovery and self-service troubleshooting
signals.summary: Users encounter broken links (404 for provider list), missing UI elements (no Ask AI button despite issue template referencing it), low contrast search box, and undocumented features (configs directory structure, dynamic model fetching, Mercury-2 provider). These collectively impede onboarding and self-service support.
aliases: missing Ask AI button on docs
signals.review_reason: Six distinct documentation gaps were reported. The broken provider list link is a direct self-service blocker (users cannot find provider information). The missing 'Ask AI' button means users cannot follow the recommended troubleshooting path before filing issues. Low contrast search impairs the core docs navigation. Undocumented features (configs directory, model refresh, Mercury-2) prevent user discovery of functionality they already have. Collectively these represent significant barriers to onboarding and support self-service.

source_issues.title: No full list of provider
source_issues.evidence: VSCode extension links to 'full list of providers' but link leads to 404 page

source_issues.title: No 'Ask AI' button on the documentation
source_issues.evidence: Issue template references 'Ask AI' button but no such button exists on the main docs page; users cannot check this box when filing issues

source_issues.title: Docs: Document .continue/configs directory support
source_issues.evidence: Support for .continue/configs/ was added but never documented; users don't understand differences between configs/, agents/, assistants/ directories

source_issues.title: Low contrast on the search box
source_issues.evidence: Search box on docs.continue.dev has very low contrast text and distracting animated background; hard to read

source_issues.title: Docs: Document dynamic model fetching feature
source_issues.evidence: Dynamic model fetching (refresh button to fetch available models) was added but has no user-facing documentation; users don't know it exists or which providers support it

source_issues.title: Docs: Update Inception provider documentation for Mercury-2 model
source_issues.evidence: Mercury-2 model (128k context, tool calling) was added but docs use generic placeholders without mentioning specific models or capabilities

signals.topic: PR checks reuse stale task IDs on PR updates, causing misleading CI feedback and wasted debugging time
signals.summary: When a PR is updated (pull_request.synchronize), Continue re-posts the original PR-open check agent sessions to the new head commit instead of creating fresh sessions. This means checks report stale results on updated diffs, and the normal `cn checks reject` path cannot dismiss them because suggestionStatus=null and diff=null. Users reported spending hours debugging based on incorrect CI feedback.
aliases: PR checks stale on synchronize event
checks report stale diff on PR update
signals.review_reason: PR checks are a core CI workflow feature. When updated PRs report stale results instead of re-evaluating the new diff, users cannot trust CI feedback, leading to wasted debugging hours. This is a direct main-flow blocking issue for users relying on Continue checks for PR quality gates.

source_issues.title: PR checks do not create fresh agent sessions on PR updates; stale task IDs re-post to new commits
source_issues.evidence: 6 hours of misleading CI feedback; same task IDs reused across all commits; failed Anti-Slop status described original issue not fixed diff; normal `cn checks reject` path cannot dismiss stale state; user wasted significant debugging time

signals.topic: Terminal commands fail for tcsh/csh users due to hardcoded -l shell flag
signals.summary: Continue hardcodes the `-l` (login shell) flag for all Unix shells when executing terminal commands. tcsh and csh do not support `-l`, causing every terminal command to fail with 'Unknown option: -l'. This completely breaks terminal command execution for affected users.
signals.review_reason: Terminal command execution is a fundamental feature. When all terminal commands fail immediately for any user whose shell is tcsh or csh (a common configuration in academic/scientific environments), the tool is effectively broken for those users. The failure is total and non-recoverable without a code change.

source_issues.title: Terminal commands fail when $SHELL is set to tcsh due to hardcoded -l shell flag
source_issues.evidence: Every terminal command fails with 'Unknown option: -l' when $SHELL=/bin/tcsh; exit code 1 for basic commands (pwd, ls, echo); tcsh and csh do not support the -l flag but Continue hardcodes it for all Unix shells

signals.topic: Opaque config validation error prevents setup, no actionable error message
signals.summary: When a user has an invalid Ollama Cloud configuration, Continue shows 'Failed to parse config: models.0: Invalid input' with no specifics about which field is wrong or what value is expected. The user cannot diagnose or fix the issue, and the extension may be in a broken state.
signals.review_reason: Config setup is a blocking prerequisite for using Continue. When validation fails with an opaque error and provides no field-level detail, users cannot self-serve a fix. This blocks the core setup flow, especially for users trying to configure Ollama Cloud for the first time.

source_issues.title: Config error with ollama cloud
source_issues.evidence: Error message 'Failed to parse config: models.0: Invalid input' provides no actionable detail; user explicitly asks 'How do I know what the error is so I can fix it?'; extension appears to be in broken state with no recovery path

signals.topic: JetBrains plugin crashes on startup due to OutOfMemoryError in Gson.toJson
signals.summary: The JetBrains plugin crashes on startup with java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space in Dispatchers.IO. The crash originates from Gson.toJson in ContinueBrowser.sendToWebview. The plugin is completely unusable for affected JetBrains users.
signals.review_reason: Plugin crash on startup is a complete feature unavailability issue. The JetBrains plugin becomes entirely unusable — not degraded functionality but total failure. OOM during JSON serialization indicates a memory management bug triggered by user data (message history, config size), making it a reproducible failure for users with typical amounts of data.

source_issues.title: crash
source_issues.evidence: Unhandled exception java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space in Dispatchers.IO on startup; crash in Gson.toJson in ContinueBrowser.sendToWebview; plugin completely unusable for affected users

signals.topic: Mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency breaks installation on all Intel Macs (macOS x86_64)
signals.summary: crewai 1.12.2 declares lancedb>=0.29.2 as a mandatory core dependency. lancedb dropped macOS x86_64 wheel builds at 0.29.2, making crewai uninstallable on all Intel Macs — even for projects that never use memory features. The workaround (--no-deps) is not viable.
signals.review_reason: Hard installation failure on an entire platform (Intel Macs). User cannot install crewai at all. Confirmed via uv pip resolver with explicit platform tag mismatch. pyproject.toml shows lancedb is a mandatory (not optional) dependency despite memory features being non-essential.

source_issues.title: [BUG] crewai 1.12.2 uninstallable on Intel Macs: mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2  dependency has no macOS x86_64 wheels
source_issues.evidence: pip install crewai==1.12.2 and uv pip install 'lancedb>=0.29.2' both fail on Intel Mac with ResolutionImpossible. The error explicitly lists available platforms (macosx_11_0_arm64 only) and confirms macOS x86_64 is absent. pyproject.toml line 44 hardcodes lancedb>=0.29.2 as a mandatory (non-optional) dependency.

signals.topic: OpenAI API key works outside CrewAI but fails with 401 inside CrewAI Studio subprocess execution
signals.summary: The same valid OpenAI API key works in standalone Python/curl tests but fails with 401 invalid_api_key when CrewAI Studio builds and executes the crew in a subprocess. Tool validation succeeds but agent LLM calls fail, with VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch warning in logs.
aliases: api key auth fails in subprocess
signals.review_reason: Primary workflow (crew.kickoff()) is blocked by authentication failure. A valid API key is rejected inside the CrewAI subprocess even though it works in the same environment outside CrewAI. This is a critical regression for CrewAI Studio users — the entire crew execution pipeline fails.

source_issues.title: [BUG] OpenAI API key works locally but fails inside CrewAI with 401 invalid_api_key
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace shows crew.kickoff() fails with openai.AuthenticationError 401. Logs show 'OpenAI: Successfully validated tool' (tools work) but then 'ERROR:root API call failed: Error code: 401'. Same key works in standalone Python client and curl. Log shows VIRTUAL_ENV=/data/internal/venv does not match project environment path /shared_venv — key is not propagated into subprocess. User hypothesis: CrewAI not correctly propagating OPENAI_API_KEY to the subprocess runtime.

signals.topic: HITL pre-review with learn=True silently fails open: exceptions swallowed, no warning, no safeguards applied
signals.summary: When @human_feedback(learn=True) recalls lessons and the pre-review LLM call fails (network, auth, LLM error, structured-output), the except block returns raw method_output without propagating any exception, logging any warning, or informing downstream components. Users cannot distinguish reviewed from unreviewed output.
signals.review_reason: Safety-critical silent bypass in human-in-the-loop workflow. When pre-review fails (network, auth, LLM error), the system continues as if it succeeded — no exception, no warning. Callers receive what appears to be reviewed output but is actually raw model output. This defeats the entire purpose of human feedback safeguards.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: HITL pre-review fails open and silently bypasses automated safeguards
source_issues.evidence: Code analysis shows _pre_review_with_lessons catches all exceptions and returns original method_output. No exception propagated, no warning logged, no error signal. Downstream callers cannot distinguish pre-reviewed output from raw model output. Step-by-step reproduction provided. Expected: fail-closed or explicit degradation with logging.

signals.topic: output_pydantic causes tools to be skipped on all non-OpenAI LLMs (vLLM, LiteLLM) since v1.9.0
signals.summary: Since v1.9.0, Task.output_pydantic is passed as response_format into the agent tool-calling loop on every iteration. For vLLM and other OpenAI-compatible servers, this causes models to skip tool calls entirely and return structured JSON directly. Tools are never invoked. This is a confirmed regression from the 'Structured outputs' change in v1.9.0.
signals.review_reason: Core feature regression: output_pydantic (a major v1.9.0 feature) silently breaks tool execution for the entire non-OpenAI LLM ecosystem. Users of vLLM, LiteLLM, and other OpenAI-compatible providers cannot use tools + structured output simultaneously. However, this affects a specific combination (output_pydantic + non-OpenAI LLM), not all users.

source_issues.title: [BUG] `output_pydantic` / `response_model` leaks into agent tool-calling loop, causing tools to be skipped on non-OpenAI LLMs
source_issues.evidence: Minimal reproduction provided: with output_pydantic=MyOutput, AddTool._run() is never called. Verified via curl that vLLM with both tools and response_format skips tool_calls and returns direct JSON. LiteLLM path in llm.py _handle_non_streaming_response() makes a separate LLM call with NO tools at all when response_model is set. Pre-v1.9.0 behavior (post-processing via Task._export_output) worked correctly. Gemini already has a provider-specific workaround acknowledging this conflict.

signals.topic: BrightData SERP tool uses JS template literal syntax in Python f-strings, generating malformed search URLs for all queries
signals.summary: The get_search_url method in BrightDataSearchTool uses ${query} (JavaScript template literal syntax) instead of {query} (Python f-string syntax), prepending a literal $ to every query. All three search engines (Google, Bing, Yandex) produce broken URLs like https://www.google.com/search?q=$AI%20news instead of https://www.google.com/search?q=AI%20news.
signals.review_reason: BrightData SERP tool is completely broken — every search query generates a malformed URL with a '$' prefix, causing all searches to fail. This affects all three supported search engines. Though a single-issue bug, it completely breaks the primary function of the BrightDataSearchTool for every user.

source_issues.title: [BUG] BrightData SERP tool uses JavaScript template syntax in Python f-strings, breaking all search queries
source_issues.evidence: Every search query gets prepended with '$'. Example: 'AI news' becomes 'https://www.google.com/search?q=$AI%20news'. All three search engines affected. Confirmed as a template literal vs f-string syntax error in code.

signals.topic: CLI hangs indefinitely ("Thinking...") with auto model selection and Gemini Pro variants
signals.summary: CLI hangs at 'Thinking...' stage indefinitely with no timeout, blocking all user interactions. Observed across auto model selection and specific Pro model variants (gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview), lasting from minutes to 33+ minutes.
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports of CLI hanging at 'Thinking...' with no timeout. Issue #26915 is explicitly labeled long-standing since v0.3.x, indicating systemic failure. The block is recoverable when it eventually resolves but can waste 20-33+ minutes of user time, representing significant UX degradation and workflow interruption. Count=3 meets P1 threshold.

signals.summary: CLI generates malformed message history with multiple consecutive function responses, causing Gemini API to reject requests with 400 'function call turn comes immediately after a user turn' errors and breaking tool execution mid-conversation.
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues both show API 400 errors caused by malformed request bodies. The CLI violates Gemini API's strict role-alternation requirements during tool execution, causing the primary workflow to fail. Not P0 because count=2 is below the frequency threshold and the 400s are recoverable (vs. permanently blocking).

signals.summary: As conversation context grows, even trivial operations like staged commit-and-push take 7+ minutes, making the CLI impractical for iterative development workflows.
signals.review_reason: User reports a 7+ minute execution time for what should be a seconds-long operation. The degradation is explicitly correlated with conversation length (context size), indicating a systemic scaling problem. This is P1 despite count=1 because the impact is severe (blocks core development workflow) and the pattern (context-length correlation) suggests a reproducible systemic issue rather than an isolated incident.

signals.summary: Users receive 429 rate limit errors after using less than 10% of their quota, causing the CLI to hang indefinitely with no user-visible error, making the tool unusable despite having available credits.
signals.review_reason: Despite count=1, this is a P1 because: (1) the tool becomes completely unusable with credits still available, representing a false-positive quota exhaustion; (2) the 429 error is invisible to the user (only in debug log), making diagnosis impossible; (3) it causes indefinite hangs of up to an hour. This creates significant confusion and wasted time, qualifying as a major UX and functional issue.

signals.topic: Uncontrolled memory consumption spikes when pasting large content (1GB to 12GB)
signals.summary: CLI memory consumption spikes from ~1GB to 12GB when processing large error traces or content, causing significant resource exhaustion and potential OOM crashes on memory-constrained systems.
signals.review_reason: Memory consumption increased 12x (1GB to 12GB) from a single paste operation, confirming unbounded memory growth. On memory-constrained systems this can cause OOM crashes (workstation/app termination). The CLI version (0.41.2) and auto-gemini-3 model are the latest stable, indicating this affects production users. P1 despite count=1 due to the severity of resource exhaustion.

source_issues.title: Memory Leak

signals.topic: TransformersModel does not forward quantization_config parameter, blocking 8-bit/4-bit model loading on memory-constrained GPUs
signals.summary: TransformersModel class does not pass the quantization_config parameter to AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(), preventing users from loading quantized models (8-bit/4-bit via BitsAndBytes) on GPU. Users attempting to use quantization to fit large models in limited GPU memory observe that models are still loaded in full precision, exhausting VRAM.
aliases: BitsAndBytes 8-bit quantization not working in smolagents
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed functional bug with reproducible impact: quantization_config is silently ignored by TransformersModel, causing GPU out-of-memory errors for users who expect 8-bit quantization to work. The user's workflow is blocked — they cannot run agents with large models on typical consumer GPUs. Evidence is explicit in the issue body with code reproduction and observed memory behavior.

source_issues.title: [BUG] quantization_config is not supported in TransformersModel
source_issues.evidence: User provides reproducible code: passing BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_8bit=True) to TransformersModel has no effect; model does not fit in GPU memory despite quantization config being set. The root cause is that TransformersModel does not forward quantization_config to the underlying AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained() call.

signals.topic: SkillsMiddleware skips loading skills on first agent turn due to empty list default for skills_metadata
signals.summary: SkillsMiddleware checks `if 'skills_metadata' in state` but PrivateStateAttr defaults this field to [], so the key always exists on the first turn. The guard fires on the empty list, _list_skills_with_errors is never called, and the agent shows '(No skills available yet)' even though valid skills exist on disk.
signals.review_reason: This is a functional bug that causes key skills to be completely unavailable on the first agent turn. Users who configure skills following the documented pattern get '(No skills available yet)' on first invocation, even though skills exist on disk and work on subsequent turns. Three independent reports confirm the same root cause. Priority P1 (not P0) because it self-resolves on subsequent turns and is gated on a specific initialization condition.

source_issues.title: SkillsMiddleware skips loading skills on first turn when skills_metadata=[] (PrivateStateAttr default)
source_issues.evidence: Bug with minimal repro: create agent with skills=['/skills/'] pointing to valid SKILL.md, invoke agent, system prompt shows '(No skills available yet)'. Root cause: guard `if 'skills_metadata' in state` fires on empty list from PrivateStateAttr default. Proposed fix provided.

source_issues.title: SkillsMiddleware skips loading skills on first turn when skills_metadata=[] (PrivateStateAttr default)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report confirming the same bug: first invocation always skips skill loading because skills_metadata key exists with empty list value.

source_issues.title: SkillsMiddleware skips loading on first turn when skills_metadata=[] (PrivateStateAttr default)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report. Steps: create agent with skills=['/skills/'] pointing to valid SKILL.md, invoke agent, system prompt shows '(No skills available yet)'. Root cause and fix identical to #3235.

signals.topic: MCP pre-flight HEAD request silently drops authentication headers, causing all authenticated MCP servers to fail
signals.summary: The `_check_remote_server` function sends a HEAD request without passing configured auth headers from the MCP server config, so any MCP server requiring API key/token authentication returns HTTP 500 and is silently skipped. Users cannot use any MCP server with authentication.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear workflow-blocking bug. The MCP pre-flight check silently skips ALL authenticated MCP servers, meaning any user who configures an MCP server requiring API key or token authentication cannot use it at all. The failure is silent (no error shown to user, server just disappears from the agent), making it especially harmful. Two independent reports confirm the same root cause (missing headers in HEAD request at mcp_tools.py:861). The bug is reproducible and the user impact is explicitly stated in both reports.

source_issues.title: MCP pre-flight HEAD request missing authentication headers
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with full reproduction: HEAD request at mcp_tools.py:861 sends no headers. Authenticated MCP servers return HTTP 500 and are silently skipped. Impact stated explicitly: 'All authenticated MCP servers (requiring API keys/tokens) fail pre-flight and are silently skipped.'

source_issues.title: MCP pre-flight HEAD request missing authentication headers
source_issues.evidence: Detailed duplicate report with Python repro script demonstrating that HEAD request without headers returns 500 while same request with headers returns 200. Impact: 'Users cannot use authenticated MCP servers with DeepAgents CLI.'

signals.topic: SubAgent response_format causes intermediate HITL/tool calls to produce malformed payloads
signals.summary: When response_format is set on a SubAgent, provider-native structured output binding is applied to every model call inside the subagent, not just the final response. This causes intermediate tool calls (including human-in-the-loop/approval tools) to receive empty or null fields instead of expected structured data, breaking approval workflows.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-affecting bug for users who use SubAgent response_format with intermediate tools or HITL approval flows. The same subagent with response_format produces corrupted intermediate tool calls (null fields, empty objects) that would cause incorrect user-facing approval UIs or silent data loss. Two reports with full repros. Priority P1 because not all subagent users have intermediate tools, but it is a significant regression for those who do.

source_issues.title: SubAgent response_format affects intermediate tool/HITL calls
source_issues.evidence: Bug with full Python repro showing that the same subagent produces valid ask_human structured_data without response_format but produces summary=null and options=[{}] with response_format. HITL/approval tool calls are corrupted. Related to #2512 and #330.

source_issues.title: SubAgent response_format affects intermediate tool/HITL calls
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate with detailed technical analysis. Root cause: `_get_bound_model()` applies provider structured-output kwargs on every subagent model call, not just the final one. Shows two failure modes: tool schema validation fails, or intermediate tool args are malformed.

signals.topic: CompositeBackend write/edit emits spurious DeprecationWarning on every call via dataclasses.replace
signals.summary: Every call to CompositeBackend.write or CompositeBackend.edit triggers a LangChainDeprecationWarning for the deprecated `files_update` field, because dataclasses.replace() re-passes the deprecated field back through __init__. This floods logs with warnings and degrades the developer experience for every user of CompositeBackend.
signals.review_reason: This is a real bug causing noisy, misleading warnings on every write/edit operation through CompositeBackend. While it doesn't block the write itself (the operation completes), it floods user logs with spurious deprecation warnings pointing at the library's own code, degrading trust and making real warnings harder to spot. Only one report but root cause is clearly identified and easily reproducible.

source_issues.title: CompositeBackend.write/edit emits self-induced files_update DeprecationWarning via dataclasses.replace
source_issues.evidence: Bug with minimal repro: backend.write('/tmp.txt', 'hello') emits LangChainDeprecationWarning for 'files_update'. Root cause: WriteResult/EditResult __init__ warns when files_update is passed, but dataclasses.replace() re-passes all fields including files_update=None. Workaround suggested by user.

signals.topic: Multi-turn tool-calling conversations with Gemini via ChatOpenAI crash with 400 BadRequestError due to missing thought_signature
signals.summary: When using Gemini models through ChatOpenAI in multi-turn agentic conversations with tools, follow-up turns fail with 400 BadRequestError because thought_signature is not passed in followup turns.
aliases: ChatOpenAI Gemini thought signature missing multi-turn
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow blocking bug: multi-turn tool-calling with Gemini via ChatOpenAI crashes with 400 error, making Gemini tool use completely unusable in conversational agent workflows. User provides explicit error message and minimal reproduction case.

source_issues.title: ChatOpenAI fails to provide thought signatures on multi-turn conversations when used with Gemini models, resulting in 400 BadRequestError
source_issues.evidence: Error: 'Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts. This is required for tools to work correctly.' User provides minimal repro. Blocks multi-turn agentic workflows with Gemini tool use.

signals.topic: SSRF protection bypass in validate_safe_url when LANGCHAIN_ENV set to any 'local*' value (including local_test, local_staging)
signals.summary: validate_safe_url uses startswith('local') check and a startswith('test')+hostname contains 'server' bypass, allowing attacker-controlled URLs to bypass SSRF validation in local/test environments.
signals.review_reason: SSRF bypass allows internal network access through a trivial environment-variable manipulation. 12 comments indicate active community engagement and real-world exploitation attempts. While count=1, the vulnerability is exploitable with a one-line change and can lead to data exfiltration from internal services.

source_issues.title: Bug: SSRF bypass in validate_safe_url when LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test
source_issues.evidence: validate_safe_url('http://test.attacker.server.com/exfil') returns attacker URL instead of raising ValueError when LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test. Also _effective_allowed_hosts() uses startswith('local') incorrectly allowing env vars like 'local_staging'. 12 comments indicating active community discussion and real exploitation risk.

signals.topic: Arbitrary file read via path traversal in Chroma.add_images() through unsanitized URI input
signals.summary: Chroma.add_images() passes URIs directly to Path(uri).open('rb') without sanitization, enabling path traversal attacks (e.g. ../../../../etc/passwd) that read and return arbitrary files base64-encoded through the embeddings pipeline.
signals.review_reason: Path traversal in Chroma integration allows arbitrary file system read through a single URI parameter change. No path validation exists. While count=1, the impact is severe (arbitrary file read) with a trivial exploitation path and no existing safeguards.

source_issues.title: Bug: path traversal in Chroma.add_images() via unsanitized URI
source_issues.evidence: store.add_images(uris=['../../../../etc/passwd']) reads arbitrary files and returns base64-encoded content. Root cause: encode_image() calls Path(uri).open('rb') with no path validation. 7 comments with community discussion and clear repro.

signals.topic: Subgraph stream events silently dropped when reconnecting with stream_mode filter
signals.summary: When a client reconnects to a LangGraph stream via joinStream with a stream_mode filter, all subgraph events are silently dropped. The root cause is a read-side filter mismatch: the write path uses prefix matching (e.g., base mode 'updates' matches 'updates|subgraph:abc'), but the read path uses exact string equality, causing subgraph modes to fail the filter and be silently discarded. Users lose all subgraph event data on reconnection.
aliases: stream_mode filter drops subgraph events on reconnect
signals.review_reason: Silently drops subgraph events on stream reconnection — a data-loss regression in a core streaming API. Users cannot retrieve subgraph state after disconnect, breaking resumable workflows. Clear reproduction, root cause identified in code, no workaround for affected versions.

source_issues.title: langgraph-runtime-inmem: Runs.Stream.join drops subgraph events when stream_mode is supplied (joinStream regression)
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction with minimal 3-file setup; assertion proves joinStream returns 0 subgraph events while initial stream returns 12. Filter uses exact equality on compound mode strings (e.g., 'updates|subgraph:abc') instead of matching base mode.

signals.topic: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud, causing duplicate work and cost
signals.summary: On LangGraph Cloud, tool calls taking more than ~180 seconds are silently re-dispatched from checkpoint while the original is still running. The root cause traces to a 120-second hardcoded heartbeat interval in langgraph-api: BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120 causes the sweep task to run every 240s and call Runs.Sweep(), which marks apparently-stale runs as retriable. Both the original and duplicate complete successfully, resulting in 2-3x redundant LLM calls and compute cost. No existing workarounds (BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS, BG_JOB_ISOLATED_LOOPS) resolve the issue.
signals.review_reason: Causes 2-3x actual cost increase from duplicate LLM calls in production. Silent failure — users are unaware duplicate work is being done. Affects a core use case (legitimately long-running tool calls). Multiple workarounds attempted and failed.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: 17 comments from multiple users confirming duplicate runs with identical tool call hashes, no preceding model node on duplicates, consistent across langgraph 1.1.3-1.1.6 on EU Cloud Plus tier. Root cause traced to hardcoded BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120 and retriable CancelledError. Cost impact: 2-3x redundant LLM calls.

signals.topic: langgraph dev ignores checkpointer configuration, forcing in-memory storage and losing all state on restart
signals.summary: The `langgraph dev` command forcibly uses the in-memory runtime (langgraph_runtime_inmem) regardless of any checkpointer configured in the code. This causes complete loss of conversation state on every server restart, even when users explicitly configure persistent checkpointers like AsyncSqliteSaver. All state is lost on restart; the .langgraph_api directory is not used for persistence. This makes development of stateful conversational agents extremely difficult, as any hot reload triggers state loss.
aliases: langgraph dev loses state on restart
signals.review_reason: Complete state loss on restart is a primary workflow blocker. `langgraph dev` is the standard development entry point, and losing all conversation state on every restart makes iterative development of stateful agents impractical. Count=1 but P0 because (a) it's the primary dev workflow, (b) state loss is total and permanent, (c) workaround requires switching to production deployment for basic state testing.

source_issues.title: `langgraph dev` Ignores Checkpointer Configuration, Forcing In-Memory Storage and Preventing State Persistence
source_issues.evidence: 11 comments from users confirming state loss on every restart. Explicitly demonstrated with SQLite checkpointer — checkpoint.db is created but empty after restart. Startup logs confirm 'Using langgraph_runtime_inmem'. Blocks development of stateful agents.

signals.topic: Checkpoint serialization failure when nested agents return AIMessage — TypeError not msgpack serializable
signals.summary: When a parent StateGraph uses a nested sub-agent (via create_react_agent) and that sub-agent returns an AIMessage as part of its output, the checkpoint write fails with TypeError: 'Type is not msgpack serializable: AIMessage'. This occurs in the checkpoint serialization pipeline (serde/jsonplus.py -> msgpack) during the nested agent's invoke call. The error blocks the parent graph from using checkpointing entirely when nested agents are involved, preventing state persistence and resumability.
aliases: AIMessage not msgpack serializable in checkpoint
signals.review_reason: Prevents checkpointing entirely when using the extremely common nested agent pattern (create_react_agent inside a StateGraph node). Full stack trace with clear root cause in serialization layer. 22 comments from users hitting the same pattern. Blocks state persistence for a core multi-agent pattern.

source_issues.title: TypeError: Type is not msgpack serializable: AIMessage
source_issues.evidence: 22 comments from multiple users hitting the same error with nested agent patterns. Full stack trace from checkpoint/serde/jsonplus.py:219 showing ormsgpack.packb failure. Common pattern: create_react_agent called inside a parent StateGraph node, returning messages with AIMessage objects.

signals.topic: langgraph dev port binding fails with TIME-WAIT socket conflict, blocking rapid server restarts
signals.summary: After stopping `langgraph dev` with Ctrl+C, the server cannot be restarted on port 2024 for ~60 seconds due to TCP TIME-WAIT state. The port resolution code in langgraph_api/cli.py (_resolve_port) does not use SO_REUSEADDR, causing bind() to fail even though no process is LISTEN-ing. This blocks iterative development workflows requiring rapid restart cycles, forcing developers to either wait 60s or use a different port each time.
aliases: Port 2024 already in use after Ctrl+C
signals.review_reason: Blocks the primary development restart cycle, forcing 60-second waits or manual port management. Clear root cause with a one-line fix (SO_REUSEADDR). Frequent developer friction in iterative development. P1 rather than P0 because the workaround (wait or change port) prevents complete workflow stoppage.

source_issues.title: `langgraph dev` falsely reports 'Port 2024 already in use' due to TIME-WAIT entries
source_issues.evidence: Full OSError stack trace from langgraph_api/cli.py:_resolve_port. Root cause identified as missing SO_REUSEADDR in socket bind. Proposed fix with code patch. Blocks dev restart workflow — must wait ~60s or use different port.

signals.topic: SQLAlchemy session transaction conflict in RAG Pipeline causes dataset creation/import to fail with null redirect

rag pipeline dsl service transaction error

npm package missing compiled dist output
