source_issues.title: @mem0/openclaw-mem0: published package ships unbuilt TypeScript; bricks OpenClaw gateway after recent plugin-validation tightening
source_issues.evidence: 安装插件后openclaw gateway启动直接报错'Invalid config...requires compiled runtime output'，openclaw doctor --fix无法自动修复，用户需手动tsdown编译，但重新安装后问题复现，完全阻断Gateway启动流程。

signals.topic: addMemory流程的metadata字段（如app_id）未参与检索过滤与消息分区隔离，导致多app场景下跨上下文记忆污染
signals.summary: Memory.add()的Phase1检索和SQLite消息分区将search_filters限制为仅user_id/agent_id/run_id三个字段，metadata被排除在外。这意味着同一user_id在不同app_id下的记忆窗口和候选池相互共享，Memory.search却能正确传递完整filters到向量层，造成严重的不一致性与跨上下文污染风险。
signals.review_reason: 多app部署场景下核心记忆检索逻辑存在设计缺陷，导致同一用户在不同应用间的记忆互相污染，关键检索功能不可靠。issue#5121提供了可复现代例，bug标签确认，Memory.search与Memory.add行为不一致有明确技术分析，影响明确但count=1故降为P1。

source_issues.title: `addMemory` flow excludes `metadata` (e.g. `app_id`) from retrieval and message partitioning, causing cross-context contamination in multi-app setups
source_issues.evidence: 提供了可复现的代码示例，证明app-a和app-b在同一user_id下共享消息窗口，Phase1检索返回的记忆被跨app混入，且与Memory.search的filter行为不一致。

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock客户端缺少boto3超时配置，大型记忆处理触发Read timeout阻断生产流程
signals.summary: AWSBedrockLLM类创建boto3客户端时未传递timeout配置，使用默认60秒超时。当处理大型记忆或复杂记忆提取时，boto3 read timeout错误频发，无任何配置手段可调高超时时间，AWS官方建议大型模型查询超时应为3600秒，用户被完全阻断。
signals.review_reason: 虽然labels含enhancement，但issue包含明确的Read timeout生产错误日志，说明用户在处理大型记忆时直接遭遇生产阻断。AWSBedrockLLM无任何超时配置手段，AWS官方文档建议3600秒但代码硬编码默认60秒，用户无法完成大型记忆操作，符合P1标准。

source_issues.title: Add boto3 timeout configuration support for AWS Bedrock client
source_issues.evidence: Issue包含完整错误日志'Failed to generate response: Read timeout on endpoint URL: https://bedrock-runtime.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/model/...'，明确了生产环境中大型记忆处理的真实阻断场景。

signals.topic: DockerHub上的mem0/mem0-api-server镜像长期未更新（自2025年9月起），导致用户持续使用含有已修复Bug的旧版本
signals.summary: DockerHub上mem0/mem0-api-server镜像自2025年9月后未更新，源码中已修复的Bug（如update_memory API参数类型问题）未同步到镜像中。用户自动拉取镜像时会遇到已知的源码级已修复问题，无法通过镜像方式快速部署，被迫选择手动克隆server源码或限制使用SDK语言。
aliases: OSS API server Docker image stale
signals.review_reason: Docker镜像长期（超8个月）未同步源码更新，用户自动拉取时会遇到源码级已修复的Bug。虽count=1但影响持续且明确：用户被迫放弃Docker部署方式或手动维护，失去自动化的核心价值，属持续性体验下降。

source_issues.title: Why has the Dockerhub Image for the OSS Rest API not been updated
source_issues.evidence: 作者明确指出Dockerhub镜像自2025年9月起未更新，源码已修复的update_memory API bug未体现在镜像中，列举了具体影响：用户无法通过自动拉取方式获得最新修复版本，被迫手动维护。

signals.topic: 企业用户因数据泄露风险无法在本地测试mem0，缺乏无外部调用/遥测的本地运行路径
signals.summary: 企业用户在测试mem0时发现API调用会暴露内部源码和技术栈，需经过安全和法律审计才能使用。虽有通过Docker+FAISS+Ollama的本地运行方案，但需要较多手动配置，缺乏清晰的本地测试路径，企业测试门槛高。
signals.review_reason: 企业用户因数据安全顾虑无法直接通过API测试mem0，需安全/法律审计，成为企业采用的门控因素。issue提供了workaround（本地Docker+FAISS+Ollama），但需大量手动配置，缺乏官方文档指引，体验显著下降，定为P2。

source_issues.title: Local mode
source_issues.evidence: 企业用户明确表示'can't have our agent call the mem0 api and leak source code or knowledge about internal tech w/o a significant and time consuming security and legal audit'，说明现有使用路径需要安全审计成为实际阻断因素。

signals.topic: Python Anthropic provider: multiple bugs in thinking blocks, function limit fallback, and beta flags handling
signals.summary: Three separate bugs in the Python Anthropic provider: (1) signature-only thinking blocks serialize with null thinking value and are rejected by Anthropic; (2) function invocation loop hitting max calls/iterations returns blank response; (3) per-run additional_beta_flags leak into request kwargs causing TypeError. All three are runtime failures that prevent agents from completing requests.
aliases: Python Anthropic thinking blocks null serialization
Anthropic empty response on function limit fallback
Python Anthropic beta flags kwarg leak
signals.review_reason: Three independent bugs in the same provider (Python Anthropic) all causing runtime failures that prevent agent requests from completing. Issue #5783 causes API rejection on replay, #5769 produces silent blank responses to users, and #5764 causes a TypeError crash. With count=3 from the same provider all labeled as bugs, this represents a systemic reliability issue for Anthropic users.

source_issues.title: Python Anthropic: signature-only thinking blocks replay as invalid null thinking
source_issues.evidence: Content.from_text_reasoning(text=None, protected_data=...) serializes to {"type": "thinking", "thinking": null, "signature": "..."} which Anthropic API rejects with error. Minimal repro code provided.

source_issues.title: Anthropic function limit fallback can return empty final response
source_issues.evidence: When function invocation loop reaches max_function_calls or max_iterations, the fallback call returns stop_reason=end_turn with empty content array, producing a blank final response to the user. Three proposed fixes documented.

source_issues.title: Python Anthropic: per-run additional_beta_flags leaks into request kwargs
source_issues.evidence: additional_beta_flags passed per-run to _prepare_betas() is not removed from final request kwargs, causing TypeError. Root cause analysis and minimal repro provided. Label: reproduced.

signals.topic: Aspire DevUI setup follows documentation but results in agent not found or 404 errors
signals.summary: Following the official Aspire DevUI README produces two distinct blocking errors: DevUI reports 'Agent agentservice not found' (error CLIENT_ERROR) or returns 404 Not Found, despite both Agent Service and DevUI showing as healthy in Aspire Dashboard. Users following the official docs cannot use DevUI at all.
aliases: Aspire DevUI broken out of the box
signals.review_reason: Two separate but highly correlated bugs where following the official Aspire DevUI documentation results in completely non-functional DevUI. The fact that both services report healthy in the dashboard while the UI is completely broken makes this a classic out-of-the-box failure. The reproduction label on both issues confirms this is a repeatable, user-blocking issue affecting the official getting-started experience.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Following the Aspire DevUI Readme results in `Error: CLIENT_ERROR: Agent 'agentservice' not found.`
source_issues.evidence: User follows official Aspire DevUI README exactly, both services show healthy in Aspire Dashboard, yet DevUI throws CLIENT_ERROR with agent not found. Full AppHost.cs and Program.cs code provided. Label: reproduced.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Following the Aspire DevUI Readme results in 404 Not Found
source_issues.evidence: User follows official Aspire DevUI README, both DevUI and Agent Service show as healthy in Aspire Dashboard, yet opening DevUI link returns 404 Not Found. Label: reproduced.

signals.topic: Multi-agent responses lose structured JSON metadata or show garbled function-calling instructions in output
signals.summary: In multi-agent orchestration, agent responses occasionally lose structured JSON metadata and return only plain text, or alternatively display garbled function-calling instructions mixed with incorrect language characters in the output. Both behaviors represent data loss in multi-agent response streams.
aliases: function calling instructions appear in agent output
garbled multi-agent output with language mixing
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but related issues: (#5785) multi-agent responses silently dropping structured JSON metadata means downstream systems relying on that data break without any error; (#5770) function calling instructions appearing in user-visible output is a quality/experience failure. Both affect the core multi-agent orchestration product. Count=2 with both labeled as bugs and one marked reproduced.

source_issues.title: Bug: Agent responses lose structured JSON metadata in multi-agent orchestration (MAF 1.x.x)
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with screenshots showing responses losing structured JSON metadata appended at the end. Observed in agent-framework-azure-ai 1.0.0b251204 and agent-framework-core 1.0.0b251204. Responses return plain text only instead of plaintext + JSON metadata.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Function Calling instructions erroneously included in the output
source_issues.evidence: Multi-agent supervisor output contains function calling instructions mixed with Thai language characters and Italian. Shows garbled JSON with to=multi_tool_use.parallel and incorrect content. Label: reproduced.

signals.topic: Blocking synchronous tool execution freezes async event loop, preventing polling in Python agent apps
signals.summary: When a tool function contains blocking synchronous code (e.g., time.sleep), it freezes the entire async event loop, blocking the Responses API from polling. Azure Bot cannot poll for new messages while the event loop is frozen, causing the agent to appear unresponsive.
aliases: Python sync tool blocking async loop
sync tools block event loop preventing polling
signals.review_reason: A synchronous tool with blocking code freezes the entire async event loop, which is a fundamental execution model conflict. This is not a rare edge case: any user who writes a sync tool that performs I/O (sleep, requests, file I/O) will hit this. The agent becomes completely unresponsive while the loop is frozen, which is a primary flow blocking issue for Python agent developers.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Blocking synchronous tool execution freezes Responses API polling inside async event loop
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows that sync tool with time.sleep(120) freezes the async event loop, blocking Azure Bot from polling Responses API. Proposed fix is to use asyncio.to_thread(). Label: reproduced.

signals.topic: .NET Magentic Orchestrator cannot send ChatMessage, blocking multi-agent setup
signals.summary: Attempting to use Magentic Orchestration in .NET produces an Executor type error: 'Executor MagenticOrchestrator cannot send messages of type Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ChatMessage'. Users trying to build multi-agent workflows with Magentic cannot run at all.
signals.review_reason: Magentic Orchestration is a supported workflow pattern in .NET, but attempting to use it causes a type incompatibility crash at runtime. Even though the issue is closed, the bug represents a complete block on using Magentic multi-agent workflows. The fact that it was closed without visible resolution in the provided data means it may still affect users.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Error while trying to use Magentic Orchestration
source_issues.evidence: Full C# code sample shows MagenticWorkflowBuilder multi-agent setup failing with: Executor MagenticOrchestrator cannot send messages of type Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ChatMessage. Label: reproduced. Issue state: closed.

signals.topic: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even (off-by-one error)
signals.summary: When using GroupChat with 3 agents and an even max_round value (e.g., max_round=4), the last agent (agent C) is never selected due to an off-by-one error in the speaker selection loop. This is a deterministic logic bug that silently breaks multi-agent round-robin workflows.
signals.review_reason: 3 identical issues filed by the same user within 2 days, all reproducible on autogen-agentchat 0.4.x. The off-by-one error in GroupChat speaker selection is a deterministic logic bug that silently breaks round-robin execution — one agent is permanently excluded from the conversation, which is a complete workflow failure for multi-agent orchestration tasks.

source_issues.title: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even
source_issues.evidence: Off-by-one error in speaker selection loop causes agent C to never speak with 3 agents and max_round=4. Reproducible with autogen-agentchat 0.4.x on Python 3.11.

source_issues.title: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even
source_issues.evidence: Identical issue: agent C never selected with 3 agents and max_round=4. Same off-by-one root cause.

source_issues.title: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even
source_issues.evidence: Identical issue: off-by-one error in speaker selection loop. Same autogen-agentchat 0.4.x environment.

signals.topic: AutoGen Studio unauthenticated RCE via WebSocket team_config (CVSS 9.8)
signals.summary: AutoGen Studio's WebSocket endpoint accepts unauthenticated team_config containing attacker-controlled Python code, leading to arbitrary code execution via FunctionTool._from_config() calling exec() on untrusted input. Default AuthConfig sets type='none', making the exploit work out-of-the-box.
signals.review_reason: Authenticated RCE with CVSS 9.8 on a default-configuration deployment is a critical user-impacting vulnerability. Any user running AutoGen Studio with default Docker settings is vulnerable to complete server compromise with no authentication required. This is not theoretical — a full PoC is provided.

source_issues.title: [Security] Critical: Unauthenticated RCE via WebSocket team_config (CVSS 9.8)
source_issues.evidence: Full server compromise via 3-step attack chain: unauthenticated WebSocket accepts team_config with malicious FunctionTool.source_code, FunctionTool._from_config() calls exec(source_code) with no sanitization or sandbox. Works with default Docker deployment configuration. CVSS 9.8, no user interaction required.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing (only UserWarning)
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it as a subprocess with no sandbox, filesystem isolation, or network restriction. The only safeguard is a UserWarning at construction time, which is easily suppressed in production environments. This enables arbitrary code execution if the LLM is manipulated via prompt injection.
signals.review_reason: While detected by a scanner rather than reported as an in-the-wild exploit, the lack of runtime enforcement (only a suppressible warning) means any user following quickstart examples or deploying with default settings is at risk of host compromise if the LLM is manipulated. This is a clear architectural gap with severe consequences (full system compromise, credential theft, lateral movement).

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with no sandbox, no filesystem isolation, no network restrictions. The only safeguard is a UserWarning that can be silently suppressed in production (e.g., -W ignore). Attack scenario: prompt injection causes LLM to generate credential exfiltration code, which executes with full host privileges. Detected by agent-audit scanner, mapped to OWASP ASI-09.

signals.topic: Custom model endpoint access blocked when http_client parameter is not serialized
signals.summary: When using autogen-ext's OpenAIChatCompletionClient with company-customized model endpoints (e.g., Azure with custom certificates), the http_client parameter is not included in serialized config. If not passed programmatically, the endpoint rejects access, blocking the entire workflow for enterprise users with custom model deployments.
aliases: custom model endpoint rejection without http_client
signals.review_reason: Enterprise users with custom model endpoints (e.g., Azure with custom TLS certificates) cannot use autogen-ext unless they programmatically pass http_client, which breaks config-file-based workflows. This is a functional blocker for custom model deployments.

source_issues.title: Add http client property in serialized config
source_issues.evidence: When using a company-customized model, the endpoint rejects access if http_client parameter is not passed. The user must pass httpx.AsyncClient(verify=False) to make Azure endpoints with custom certificates work, but http_client is not serializable in config files. This blocks the entire model integration workflow for enterprise users.

signals.topic: Structured output fails with Groq OpenAI-compatible API due to incompatible response_format.type
signals.summary: When using autogen-ext's OpenAIChatCompletionClient with Groq's OpenAI-compatible API, structured output requests fail with BadRequestError 400 because Groq does not accept 'response_format.type' values beyond ['text', 'json_object'], while AutoGen sends Pydantic model-based structured output that maps to 'json_schema' — a mode Groq does not support.
aliases: response_format json_schema not supported by Groq
signals.review_reason: Structured output is a core feature for enterprise use cases. When users connect to Groq (a popular budget-friendly LLM provider) via the OpenAI-compatible client, Pydantic-based structured output completely fails with a 400 error, making the feature unusable. This blocks structured data extraction workflows with Groq.

source_issues.title: Facing Issue while working with Groq openAI compatible endpoint
source_issues.evidence: Full traceback: openai.BadRequestError 400 with error message "'response_format.type' : value is not one of the allowed values ['text','json_object']". User is passing Pydantic model as response_format but Groq only accepts 'text' or 'json_object'. Reproducible with autogen_ext OpenAIChatCompletionClient against Groq API.

signals.topic: WebKit on Windows hangs indefinitely with authenticated CONNECT proxy (407 + socket close)
signals.summary: When an HTTP CONNECT proxy responds with 407 Proxy Authentication Required and closes the TCP socket, WebKit on Windows hangs indefinitely instead of reconnecting with credentials. Chromium handles this correctly. Blocks all WebKit test execution behind authenticated proxies on Windows.
aliases: WebKit proxy 407 credential retry failure Windows
signals.review_reason: 功能不可用：WebKit on Windows用户使用认证代理时测试完全挂起，无替代方案（Chromium工作正常）。两个issue描述同一问题（#40768和#40723），count=2。属于关键平台的关键功能失效。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WebKit on Windows hangs when CONNECT proxy closes socket after 407 doesn't reconnect with credentials
source_issues.evidence: WebKit on Windows receives 407, destroys socket, reconnects without Proxy-Authorization header, gets 407 again, and hangs indefinitely (15000ms timeout). Chromium succeeds. WebKit on Linux succeeds.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WebKit on Windows hangs when CONNECT proxy closes socket after 407 doesn't reconnect with credentials
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #40768 with full minimal repro script. WebKit hangs after proxy 407 response + socket close. No workaround available for Windows WebKit users behind authenticated proxies.

signals.topic: UI mode fails to execute tests (v1.60 regression)
signals.summary: Playwright UI mode (--ui) in version 1.60 shows failed results for every test without actually executing them, blocking the interactive debugging workflow. Tests pass normally but UI mode reports failures with empty logs.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：UI mode是Playwright的交互式调试核心功能，v1.60全面失效导致开发者无法通过GUI调试测试。降级到1.59可修复，但影响所有升级到1.60的用户。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: UI mode does not execute any tests on 1.60
source_issues.evidence: Every test executed in UI mode shows failed result with empty log/errors columns, while tests actually pass when run without --ui. Downgrade to 1.59 fixes the problem.

signals.topic: TLS handshake regression with client certificates (v1.59+)
signals.summary: Regression in v1.59.0+ causes TLS handshake failures when client certificates are configured for one domain but navigation targets a different domain. Previously worked in v1.58.0.
aliases: SSL handshake broken with client certificates regression
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断+回归问题：v1.58正常工作，v1.59+全面失效。用户报告ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED导致任何使用client certificate认证的测试流程完全失败。args=['--ignore-certificate-errors']在旧版可用但在1.59也失效。无已知workaround。

source_issues.title: [Regression]: client_certificates causing chromium to TLS handshake failure
source_issues.evidence: Regression from v1.58.0 to v1.59.0. When client certificate is set for one origin and navigation targets a different domain (which then redirects), TLS handshake fails with ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED before the redirect happens. Self-signed proxy certificate used internally by client_certificate feature is suspected as root cause.

signals.topic: playwright install hangs in Node v26
signals.summary: Playwright browser installation hangs during archive extraction when running under Node.js v26. Works correctly on Node v25 and below.
aliases: browser installation blocked on Node v26
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：新用户setup完全卡住，无法安装浏览器。Node v26已发布，用户遇到该版本时playwright无法初始化。有明确root cause（yauzl库）和已知fix，但用户需等上游或降级Node。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: playwright install hangs in node v26
source_issues.evidence: Installation works fine with Node v25 but hangs when archive extraction begins after successful download on Node v26. Root cause traced to yauzl library bug fix available at https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/yauzl/pull/168.

signals.topic: CLI file arguments with spaces in path fail on Windows
signals.summary: When passing absolute file paths containing spaces to 'npx playwright test' on Windows, tests fail to match because createFileMatcher percent-encodes spaces (%20) in file:// URLs but the regex from CLI arguments retains literal spaces.
aliases: Windows path with spaces not found
space path CLI matching broken on Windows
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（Windows特定）：路径含空格时测试完全无法运行，包括用户目录含空格的情况（'C:\Users\First Last\...'）。有明确root cause和技术细节，但属于Windows特定边缘场景。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: CLI file arguments with spaces in path fail to match on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Relative paths work; absolute paths with spaces fail with 'No tests found'. Root cause identified in createFileMatcher() Windows fallback: file:// URLs percent-encode spaces but regex retains literal spaces. Affects any CI tool passing absolute paths, including user profile dirs like 'C:\Users\First Last\...'.

signals.topic: JSON serializer enum parameter mismatch between tool schema and deserialization
signals.summary: KernelFunction schema generation uses JsonStringEnumConverter for enum parameters, but deserialization in KernelFunctionFromMethod does not — causing System.ArgumentException or JsonException at runtime when any kernel function with enum parameters is invoked.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed code-level bug where the two halves of the tool-calling pipeline use inconsistent JSON serialization. Any user who defines a kernel function with enum parameters (nested in objects or arrays) will experience silent failures and runtime exceptions. The issue is reproducible, has detailed stack traces, and marks a TODO comment in the source code acknowledging the known issue. It blocks the core tool invocation flow.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: JSON serializer options don't match between tool schema and tool calls, causing enum parameters to fail.
source_issues.evidence: Full stack traces provided: ArgumentException 'Object of type System.String cannot be converted to type TaskReminder[]' and JsonException 'The JSON value could not be converted to TaskReminder+ReminderUnit'. Confirmed in code that KernelJsonSchemaBuilder uses JsonStringEnumConverter but TryToDeserializeValue does not, breaking all enum parameter usage in kernel functions.

signals.topic: KernelJsonSchema generates duplicate 'null' type for nullable enum/int parameters with null defaults, breaking OpenAI strict mode validation
signals.summary: When a kernel function parameter is nullable enum or int with a null default value, KernelJsonSchema produces a JSON schema with 'type': ['string', 'null', 'null'] (duplicate null), causing OpenAI strict mode to reject the tool at API validation with HTTP 400 invalid_function_parameters error.
aliases: nullable enum schema duplicate null type
OpenAI strict mode tool validation failure
signals.review_reason: Root cause is a KernelJsonSchema bug that generates malformed JSON schema for nullable parameters with null defaults. While the workarounds exist (remove = null default), this breaks OpenAI strict mode which validates schemas before accepting tool calls — a critical integration path for production deployments. Single issue confirmed with exact schema diff.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Possible problem with KernelJsonSchema generation
source_issues.evidence: Schema produced: 'optionalEnumParam':{'type':['string','null','null'],'enum':['val1','val2','val3',null]} — duplicate 'null' type causes HTTP 400 invalid_function_parameters from OpenAI strict mode at the API validation stage. Repro step: define a method with nullable enum param defaulting to null, use KernelPluginFactory.CreateFromObject, call OpenAI model in strict mode.

signals.topic: OpenAI Assistant image handling throws UriFormatException due to base64 URI exceeding 65k character limit
signals.summary: When using OpenAI Assistant agents with ImageContent items, Semantic Kernel constructs a base64 data URI string that can exceed the 65k character limit of System.Uri, causing System.UriFormatException: 'Invalid URI: The Uri string is too long' and preventing assistant conversations from processing images.
aliases: OpenAI Assistant image content URI length limit
image content in assistant channel fails
signals.review_reason: Confirmed runtime crash when processing images with OpenAI Assistant — users cannot use image content with assistant-based agents. Full stack trace provided showing UriFormatException from System.Uri.CreateThis. References a known upstream workaround in the OpenAI .NET library (byte array overload) that SK should adopt. Blocks a specific but legitimate use case.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: OpenAI Assistant throws Invalid URI: The Uri string is too long.
source_issues.evidence: System.UriFormatException thrown from AssistantMessageFactory.GetMessageContents when processing ChatMessageContent with ImageContent items in an OpenAI Assistant group chat. Stack trace shows the exception originates in System.Uri.CreateThis. OpenAI .NET library has a known workaround using byte arrays, but SK does not use it.

signals.topic: Required NuGet package version unavailable on NuGet Gallery, blocking use of VectorSearchOptions in PgVector connector
signals.summary: Version 1.75.0 of Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.PgVector, which contains the VectorSearchOptions fix, is not published to NuGet Gallery, preventing users from using vector search options with the PgVector connector.
aliases: PgVector connector version 1.75.0 missing from NuGet
signals.review_reason: A specific NuGet package version containing a user-needed fix (VectorSearchOptions) is not published to NuGet Gallery, making the feature unavailable to users. This is a packaging/release distribution issue that blocks users from using a resolved feature.

source_issues.title: .Net: Missing version on Nuget Gallery for Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.PgVector
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states VectorSearchOptions is needed for their PgVector implementation, that issue is resolved in version 1.75.0, but that version is unavailable on NuGet Gallery. Points to NuGet page showing only version 1.74.0-preview available.

signals.topic: Assembly version conflicts (Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces) when using InMemory/SqliteVec connectors with .NET Framework projects
signals.summary: Referencing Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.InMemory or SqliteVec from a .NET Framework project produces MSB3277 warnings about Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces version conflicts, and at runtime throws FileLoadException due to assembly manifest mismatch, completely preventing use of the connector.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed build-time warning and runtime crash (FileLoadException) when using InMemory connector with .NET Framework. This completely blocks the connector from working on .NET Framework projects, affecting legacy enterprise scenarios. Root cause is identified as improper NuGet versioning — connector packages depend on internal packages whose versions have changed but were never published.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Assembly conflicts when referencing Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.InMemory
source_issues.evidence: Full MSB3277 warning output and FileLoadException with stack trace. Root cause identified: SK publishes connector packages without publishing their dependency packages (Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData.Abstractions) that have changed versions. The author explicitly calls out incorrect NuGet versioning strategy as the cause.

signals.topic: Codex Desktop app crashes on Windows with non-standard WSL mount paths
signals.summary: Codex Desktop crashes and fails to load on Windows when WSL uses non-standard mount paths (/c/ instead of /mnt/c/). This makes the app entirely unusable for affected Windows+WSL users.
aliases: WSL path resolution freeze on Windows-native mode
signals.review_reason: Two separate but related Windows WSL bugs: #22378 is a full crash (app won't load at all), #22378 is a startup crash blocking all usage, #22376 is a UI freeze on every codex-home request for users who have WSL_DISTRO_NAME set (even in Windows-native mode). Both are high-severity main-flow blocks on Windows with WSL users.

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop Windows - WSL - crashes on non standard mount /c instead of /mnt/c/
source_issues.evidence: Codex Desktop crashes with exit code 127: '/usr/bin/bash: line 1: /mnt/c/Users/shara/.codex/bin/wsl/codex: No such file or directory'. App does not load at all.

source_issues.title: Windows-native Codex Desktop incorrectly enables WSL path resolution when WSL_DISTRO_NAME exists, causing UI freezes
source_issues.evidence: Electron main process synchronously invokes wsl.exe for codex-home resolution, causing UI freeze for 3 seconds (cold WSL) to 100ms (warm WSL). Freeze path: 'spawnSync → wsl.exe'. WSL_DISTRO_NAME env var incorrectly triggers WSL mode in Windows-native mode.

signals.topic: CLI enters indefinite reconnect loop when model returns 404 'not found'
signals.summary: Codex CLI (gpt-5.2) returns 404 'Model not found' and enters a WebSocket/HTTPS fallback + reconnect loop, permanently blocking the main coding workflow. The 404 is a permanent error — retries are futile yet the CLI keeps retrying up to 5 times with no exit.
aliases: invalid model alias causes retry storm
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is permanently blocked: CLI fails to start a coding session and loops reconnecting. The 404 is a permanent failure (model does not exist) yet retries consume time and CPU without any chance of success. A reconnect loop with no exit condition is a full workflow block.

source_issues.title: 404 "Model not found gpt-5.2" causes WebSocket fallback + reconnect loop in Codex CLI
source_issues.evidence: CLI falls back from WebSocket to HTTPS, receives 404 'Model not found gpt-5.2', then enters 'Reconnecting... 2/5' loop indefinitely. The 404 is a permanent error — the model does not exist. The CLI retries instead of failing fast.

signals.topic: Codex Desktop repeatedly freezes and crashes on Windows, making it unusable
signals.summary: Codex Desktop on Windows repeatedly freezes showing 'Not Responding', requiring users to force-close and restart the app. The issue is frequent enough that the app is described as 'almost unusable'.
signals.review_reason: The app is repeatedly crashing/freezing on Windows in a way that makes it 'almost unusable'. This is a primary workflow block — users cannot complete coding sessions without repeated force-restarts. The severity is confirmed by the user's explicit statement that the frequency makes the app unusable, on a high-spec machine ruling out resource constraints.

source_issues.title: The Codex app on Windows is absolutely garbage.
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'The Codex app on Windows keeps freezing inexplicably, displaying "Not Responding," and I have to close and restart CodeX to fix it. This problem happens so frequently that it's almost unusable.' Affects a high-end machine (i9 CPU, 128GB RAM, Win11) — not a hardware issue.

signals.topic: Subagent review/approval requests are not clearly visible in the main thread
signals.summary: When a subagent needs user input or approval, the notification does not appear clearly in the main conversation thread on first interaction. Users may wait for long periods thinking the subagent is still running, while the review request is effectively invisible.
aliases: subagent review notification missing main thread
signals.review_reason: Blocks the code review workflow: the user has no clear signal that a subagent is waiting for their input, leading to wasted time and potentially leaving review requests unattended. Screenshots provided show the request is absent from the main thread on first interaction. This is a UX bug with real workflow impact, not merely an enhancement.

source_issues.title: Subagent review requests are not clearly surfaced in the main thread
source_issues.evidence: Subagent review request only appears in the main thread after the subagent thread has been opened once. On first interaction, the user gets no clear notification in the main thread that a review is needed. User may wait thinking subagent is still running. Screenshots show the request is absent from main thread UI.

signals.topic: Windows desktop shell resolves user PATH executables before Codex-bundled tools (rg.exe)
signals.summary: On Windows, Codex shell commands resolve executables like rg.exe from the user's PATH before using Codex's own bundled ripgrep. This causes both reliability failures (wrong rg version runs) and potential security risk (arbitrary executable could be executed instead of Codex's bundled binary).
aliases: Windows PATH precedence over bundled tools
signals.review_reason: Dual impact: (1) functional — rg fails in Codex shell, breaking search workflows; (2) security — Codex silently executes arbitrary executables from user PATH before its own bundled tools, which is a supply-chain risk. Both the reliability failure and the security concern are well-evidenced with paths and reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: Windows desktop shell resolves user PATH rg.exe before Codex-bundled rg.exe
source_issues.evidence: 'Get-Command rg' resolves to C:\Users\jim\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WinGet\Links\rg.exe (user-installed) instead of Codex's bundled ripgrep. 'rg --files' fails. Codex should either use absolute paths to bundled tools or prepend its tool directory to PATH. If a malicious 'rg.exe' is earlier on PATH, Codex would execute it silently.

signals.topic: AdvancedSQLiteSession database operations silently lose or orphan messages
signals.summary: add_items() can report success but leave messages unreadable if structure metadata write fails; delete_branch() leaves orphaned rows in agent_messages table. Both cause data loss with no clear error to callers.
aliases: SQLite session metadata write failure silent
signals.review_reason: Data integrity failures in session storage — messages are silently lost (add_items returns success but data is unreadable) or orphaned (delete_branch leaves unreachable rows). Both are clear data loss scenarios with no recoverable error signal to callers.

source_issues.title: AdvancedSQLiteSession.add_items can report success after structure metadata failure
source_issues.evidence: add_items() writes rows to base messages table and commits them, then writes structure metadata. If structure metadata write fails, add_items() logs error and returns without raising. Callers observe successful add_items() but get_items() cannot read the saved messages. Retries cannot reliably know whether to retry or stop.

source_issues.title: AdvancedSQLiteSession.delete_branch() leaves branch-only messages in the base table
source_issues.evidence: delete_branch() removes turn_usage and message_structure rows for deleted branch but leaves rows in agent_messages table when messages were only referenced by that branch. Branch-heavy sessions accumulate invisible orphaned rows causing database growth and audit noise.

signals.topic: Structured output schema corruption for Literal types and generic dict
signals.summary: AgentOutputSchema.name() crashes with AttributeError for Literal output types. AgentOutputSchema(dict[str, int]) produces wrong schema wrapping valid responses under 'response' key instead of the direct dict shape.
aliases: Literal type crash in output schema
signals.review_reason: Key structured output functionality is broken — Literal types cause a crash entirely, and generic dict types produce wrong schema causing valid model responses to be rejected. This is a core feature failure that blocks structured output use cases.

source_issues.title: AgentOutputSchema.name() fails for Literal output types
source_issues.evidence: AgentOutputSchema.name() crashes with AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute '__name__' for output types that include typing.Literal values. The schema can be built but name formatter recursively assumes every typing argument has __name__. Literal arguments are plain values such as strings, not types.

source_issues.title: Generic dict output types are wrapped under response
source_issues.evidence: AgentOutputSchema(dict[str, int]) is treated as a wrapped output type while AgentOutputSchema(dict) is not. Generic dict schema asks model to return object under 'response' instead of dict shape directly. Valid payload like {'a': 1} fails validation but {'response': {'a': 1}} is accepted.

signals.topic: Realtime known tool failures do not send model-visible output causing indefinite hang
signals.summary: When a known function tool invocation raises an exception or times out, no output is sent back to the model. The model waits indefinitely until the server-side timeout fires (~30s), causing sessions to hang silently.
aliases: Realtime tool exception no output sent
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocker in Realtime sessions — a known tool failure causes the model to hang indefinitely for ~30 seconds until timeout. This completely blocks any workflow using try/except on function tools in Realtime mode.

source_issues.title: Realtime known tool failures (exception/timeout) do not send model-visible output
source_issues.evidence: When a known function tool invocation raises an exception, no RealtimeModelSendToolOutput is sent back to the model. The model waits indefinitely for a function call result that will never arrive until the server-side timeout fires (~30 seconds). During this time the session appears to hang with no user-visible progress.

signals.topic: Local on_approval rejection reasons are dropped, model sees generic message
signals.summary: on_approval callbacks can return a rejection reason, but that reason is dropped before rejection output is generated. The run records tool call as rejected yet model-visible output falls back to a generic message.
signals.review_reason: Human-in-the-loop approval workflow is broken — when users explicitly provide rejection reasons via on_approval callback, those reasons are silently lost and the model receives a generic message instead. This breaks the clarity of approval workflows and the model's ability to understand why a tool was rejected.

source_issues.title: Local on_approval rejection reasons are dropped
source_issues.evidence: Local tool on_approval callbacks can return a rejection reason, but that reason is dropped before rejection output is generated. The run records the tool call as rejected yet the model-visible tool output falls back to a generic HITL rejection message instead of the callback's custom reason.

signals.topic: Voice text splitter drops short custom chunks causing silent content loss
signals.summary: StreamedAudioResult drops text when TTS text_splitter returns non-empty chunk shorter than 20 characters. Short responses like 'ok' are silently omitted even though the splitter explicitly marked text as ready for TTS.
signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation — silent data loss in voice streaming where short responses are completely dropped without any user notification. This breaks voice-first use cases where short acknowledgments are common.

source_issues.title: Voice text splitter drops short custom chunks
source_issues.evidence: StreamedAudioResult drops text when custom TTS text_splitter returns non-empty chunk shorter than 20 characters. This silently omits short responses such as 'ok' even though the splitter explicitly marked the text as ready for TTS. The turn_ended event is also not emitted properly, affecting lifecycle events.

signals.topic: accumulate_delta drops tool_call fragments when streaming chunks contain duplicate indexes
signals.summary: Streaming tool_call deltas with duplicate 'index' values (e.g. tool name + argument fragment in same SSE event) are stored as separate list entries instead of being merged, leaving orphaned entries and producing unparseable JSON in function.arguments. Affects vLLM with speculative decoding and other OpenAI-compatible servers.
signals.review_reason: Produces invalid JSON in tool_call.function.arguments, directly breaking tool execution downstream. Two independent reporters confirm on vLLM with speculative decoding. Valid OpenAPI spec shape that the SDK does not handle correctly.

source_issues.title: `accumulate_delta` drops tool_call fragments when one chunk has multiple entries at the same `index`
source_issues.evidence: accumulate_delta stores duplicate-index tool_calls as separate list elements, not merged. Later chunks merge into acc[0] only, leaving acc[1] orphaned. Result: function.arguments contains truncated JSON ('{"city"' instead of '{"city": "London"}'), no longer parseable.

source_issues.title: Streaming tool_call deltas with duplicate indexes in first chunk are accumulated incorrectly
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause: accumulate_delta assumes physical list position matches index field, ignores index. Produces two entries both with index:0, second entry stranded with partial arguments. Confirmed against vLLM with speculative decoding.

signals.topic: AsyncOpenAI(api_key="") raises OpenAIError in v2.34.0, breaking OpenAI-compatible local servers
signals.summary: v2.34.0 credential validation change rejects empty string api_key, breaking all local/serverless OpenAI-compatible integrations (llama.cpp, llamafile, LM Studio, vLLM) that intentionally pass api_key="". Main workflow failure with no graceful fallback.
aliases: empty api_key rejection breaking local servers
AsyncOpenAI api_key empty string v2.34.0 regression
signals.review_reason: Explicit breaking change regression: v2.34.0 blocks a common legitimate use case (OpenAI-compatible local servers) that worked in all prior versions. Workaround (passing placeholder string) is non-obvious. Represents main workflow failure for local/serverless deployments.

source_issues.title: AsyncOpenAI(api_key="") raises OpenAIError in v2.34.0, breaking OpenAI-compatible local servers
source_issues.evidence: Breaking change: v2.34.0 new credential validation now checks 'not self.api_key' (falsy for empty string) and raises OpenAIError. In v2.33.0 and all prior versions, api_key="" was silently accepted. This blocks all local server / serverless users of OpenAI-compatible endpoints (llama.cpp, llamafile, LM Studio, vLLM) who intentionally pass empty string because no auth is needed.

signals.topic: Responses API multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input
signals.summary: Passing response.output items back as input via model_dump() on reasoning models causes HTTP 400 'Unknown parameter: input[1].status' on turn 2. model_dump() fabricates output-only fields (status: None, encrypted_content: None) that the API rejects. Affects all multi-turn conversation implementations.
signals.review_reason: Main conversational workflow completely broken for reasoning models. All users attempting to implement multi-turn history via response.output passthrough encounter HTTP 400 on turn 2. Has confirmed downstream impact across multiple major projects (OpenClaw 64.9k forks, Agents SDK, pydantic-ai). Root cause unfixed for 8+ months.

source_issues.title: Responses API: multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input
source_issues.evidence: model_dump() on response.output items adds output-only fields (status: None, encrypted_content: None) which the API rejects with 400 'Unknown parameter: input[1].status'. Also affects OpenClaw (64.9k forks), Agents SDK, and pydantic-ai downstream. Root cause traced to openai/openai-openapi#536 spec issue, unfixed since Aug 2025.

signals.topic: Async Responses Structured Outputs memory leak causes unbounded RSS growth and OOM
signals.summary: Every AsyncResponses.responses.parse() call with structured outputs allocates new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer Rust objects (heavy) that are never cached or freed, because Pydantic model_rebuild fails on TypeVar-subscripted generics. In long-running servers, RSS grows linearly with request count until OOM.
signals.review_reason: Production memory leak with flame graph evidence. Every structured output parse() call leaks heavy Rust objects with no bound, guaranteed to cause OOM in any long-running server. Clear root cause identified in _parsing/_responses.py.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph confirms unbounded pydantic SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer allocation on every responses.parse() call. Root cause: Pydantic model_rebuild returns False for TypeVar-subscripted generics, preventing _built_memo cache population. RSS grows linearly; process eventually OOMs.

signals.topic: ResponseFunctionWebSearch.action type mismatch causes AttributeError on web_search_call items
signals.summary: SDK type annotation says ResponseFunctionWebSearch.action cannot be None, but the API returns action=None for some web_search_call responses. User code accessing item.action.type raises AttributeError at runtime.
aliases: web_search action type vs API mismatch
signals.review_reason: SDK type annotation contradicts actual API behavior, causing AttributeError in any user code that accesses action.type on web_search_call items. Predictable runtime crash in production code that follows the type signature.

source_issues.title: ResponseFunctionWebSearch doesn't match returned payload
source_issues.evidence: SDK type annotation implies action cannot be None, but API returns action=None for some web_search_call items (observed: last 2 of 4 searches). Code accessing item.action.type raises AttributeError. User had to add defensive 'if item.action' checks.

signals.topic: Example code imports non-existent `create_triage_agent` from `swarm.agents` module
signals.summary: The `examples/personal_shopper/main.py` example file references `from swarm.agents import create_triage_agent`, but no `swarm/agents.py` file exists in the repository. Users attempting to run the official example encounter a `ModuleNotFoundError`, blocking the basic getting-started workflow.
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete, reproducible workflow blockage: users who clone the repository and attempt to run the provided example (`examples/personal_shopper/main.py`) immediately hit a `ModuleNotFoundError` because the import `from swarm.agents import create_triage_agent` references a non-existent module. This directly breaks the main getting-started flow for new users. Count=1 is a hard constraint; it does not meet P0 criteria due to single-instance evidence, but the user impact (blocking example execution) is unambiguous and qualifies as P2.

source_issues.title: no create_triage_agent
source_issues.evidence: User reports that `examples/personal_shopper/main.py` imports `create_triage_agent` from `swarm.agents`, but `swarm/agents.py` does not exist, causing a module import error when running the example.

signals.topic: acpx sessions history API不实时反映assistant/tool事件，程序化编排时无法轮询会话进度
signals.summary: 在Codex等agent运行期间，acpx sessions history仅显示用户prompts，不显示已产生的assistant/tool条目，仅在turn结束后才完整。导致程序化编排场景下无法通过sessions history API轮询实时进度，必须直接解析rollout JSONL文件。
aliases: session history not showing live streamed events
sessions history API polling fails during active turn
signals.review_reason: 该issue在程序化编排场景下有明确用户体验影响：sessions history API无法反映实时进度，迫使消费者直接解析底层rollout JSONL文件，增加了集成复杂度，属于关键功能的可用性问题而非纯功能请求。但count=1、仅单仓，优先级定为P2。

source_issues.title: ACP session history only records prompts while Codex is running
source_issues.evidence: 用户在运行多并行Codex会话的编排场景中，sessions history API在turn进行时仅返回user prompt，已产生的assistant/tool消息不可见，但rollout JSONL文件中已有完整数据。用户被迫直接解析rollout JSONL而非使用原生API。

signals.topic: Static analysis security scanner produces false positives — multiple legitimate skills/plugins blocked from publication
signals.summary: ClawScan static analyzer flags benign skills with high-severity rules (suspicious.env_credential_access, suspicious.potential_exfiltration, suspicious.exposed_secret_literal, scanner.llm.suspicious) based on incorrect pattern detection. Multiple publishers have submitted formal appeals, indicating widespread false positive rate. Manual review is required to unblock publication.
signals.review_reason: P1 (workflow impact): Multiple legitimate, benign skills/plugins are blocked from publication by static analysis rules that produce false positives on safe patterns (env var + localhost HTTP, base64 API contract, variable names). The `false-positive` + `bug` label on #2117 confirms this is a known scanner quality issue. 6 appeals in a single file demonstrate a high false-positive rate that blocks publishers from publishing without manual review.

source_issues.title: [Skill Appeal] skillnote@0.4.0 flagged scanner.llm.suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Skill `skillnote@0.4.0` flagged for 5 intentional, documented, user-controlled behaviors (POST to user's own localhost backend, AGENTS.md graft via explicit markers, git clone of own repo, session JSONL read, daemon PID-guard). Author identifies exact root cause: scanner flags privileged behaviors rather than actual dangerous code. Companion skill `skillnote-doctor@1.0.0` scanned clean, confirming the flag targets specific capabilities, not general malware.

source_issues.title: [Review Request] Skill flagged: free-model-router-v1
source_issues.evidence: Local proxy router for free LLM models. Flagged for external HTTP calls (opt-in, disabled by default), config modification (auto-backup+rollback), localhost proxy MITM (localhost-only, auth-required), device fingerprint (one-way hash). Publisher provides detailed mitigation table and changes telemetry to opt-in. Skill does not exfiltrate user data.

source_issues.title: Request review for claw-negotiate skill flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Skill flagged for APOA-bounded SAFE negotiation via Telegram and sshsign. Publisher addressed prior findings: removed inline argv, removed font assets, added fail-closed sshsign approval, rewrote SKILL.md. Static analysis benign. VirusTotal benign. Appeal for human review.

source_issues.title: Appeal: Static analysis flag suspicious.env_credential_access on openclaw-interaction-bridge-v2 v1.6.4
source_issues.evidence: Plugin reads `OPENCLAW_APPROVAL_SECRET` env var and uses it in callback to user's own localhost gateway (`localhost:18789`). Scanner flags env var + HTTP call as credential exfiltration, but destination is the user's own machine, not a third party. VirusTotal benign, ClawScan benign. Same false-positive pattern as #1220 and #2125.

source_issues.title: Appeal: Static analysis flag suspicious.potential_exfiltration (Critical) on guanyuan-majia v1.5.3
source_issues.evidence: Skill reads `login()` parameter string, base64-encodes it (platform API contract), and POSTs to user-configured own BI host. Scanner flags base64 + HTTP as exfiltration. In reality: no local files read, destination is user's own configured host, base64 is the official Guandata BI sign-in API requirement.

source_issues.title: False positive: suspicious.exposed_secret_literal triggered by variable names, no actual secrets exposed
source_issues.evidence: Scanner flags `client.access_token = client._fetch_auth_credential()` and `self.access_token = self._fetch_auth_credential()` as critical severity. Neither line contains a hardcoded secret literal — both assign runtime function return values. Credentials actually sourced from `os.getenv()`. Rule triggers on identifier names alone (`access_token`, `secret_key`) without verifying literal assignment. Affects 3 skills: `xmind-doc-parser`, `baidu-doc-pipeline-parser`, `baidu-doc-vlm-parser`. Marked with `false-positive` and `bug` labels by maintainers.

signals.topic: GitHub OAuth login flow silently fails — callback drops auth code, preventing sign-in
signals.summary: OAuth callback redirects to app root without appending the exchange code, breaking GitHub sign-in for multiple users. Root cause: Convex Auth callback redirects to `https://clawhub.ai/` instead of `https://clawhub.ai/?code=...`, so frontend AuthCodeHandler never receives the code and cannot establish session.
signals.review_reason: P0: GitHub OAuth is the primary authentication method. When the callback drops the exchange code, users cannot sign in at all — this is a complete authentication flow failure affecting all new login attempts on affected accounts. Two independent users (#2175, #2167) confirm the same broken behavior.

source_issues.title: GitHub OAuth callback redirects to app root without exchange code, preventing login
source_issues.evidence: Convex OAuth callback `https://wry-manatee-359.convex.site/api/auth/callback/github?code=...` redirects to `https://clawhub.ai/` without `?code=...`. No JWT or refresh token stored in localStorage. GitHub sign-in cannot complete.

source_issues.title: All my skills disappeared from ClawHub + can't login (publisher: liuboacean)
source_issues.evidence: GitHub OAuth login via CLI opens browser but cannot complete flow. Publisher page shows 404. Account may be affected by prior purge/soft-delete.

signals.topic: Skills disappear from ClawHub without notification + publisher page returns 404
signals.summary: Published skills silently vanish from the catalog and direct URLs return 404, with no user notification. The publisher profile page also becomes unavailable. Root cause likely linked to account soft-delete or slug rename operations triggering unintended cascade deletion.
signals.review_reason: P0: Multiple publishers lose all their published skills with no warning or notification. Skills that were previously live at direct URLs become inaccessible. This destroys publisher work without cause and erodes trust in the platform's durability. Historical references to similar issues (#150, #1659, #79, #563) indicate a recurring systemic bug.

source_issues.title: All my skills disappeared from ClawHub + can't login (publisher: liuboacean)
source_issues.evidence: All four published skills (`zhihu-helper`, `mubu-integration`, `website-skeleton-skill`, `hermes-communication-bridge`) gone from search and direct URLs return 404. Publisher page `https://clawhub.ai/liuboacean` shows 404. Referenced #150, #1659, #79 as similar prior cases.

source_issues.title: Skills not attributed to account after reinstatement — login broken + API token revoked — @highnoonoffice
source_issues.evidence: After account reinstatement (#2039), profile page `clawhub.ai/p/highnoonoffice` shows 0 published skills despite six skill URLs returning 200 at their direct paths. Skills exist but are not connected to the account.

signals.topic: Skill publishing blocked — Convex Q(skills:checkSlugAvailability) server error
signals.summary: The 'New version' flow and 'Update skill' flow both crash with a Convex server error when checking slug availability, making it impossible to publish new versions or update existing skills. Root cause is a Convex query failure in `skills:checkSlugAvailability`.
signals.review_reason: P0: Skill publishing is a primary workflow. The `skills:checkSlugAvailability` Convex query crashes for all users attempting to update or publish skills, completely blocking the main publishing flow. Two independent users hit the exact same crash in the exact same query.

source_issues.title: [CONVEX Q(skills:checkSlugAvailability)] Server Error when updating skill
source_issues.evidence: Error: 'Something went wrong [CONVEX Q(skills:checkSlugAvailability)] [Request ID: 733d42dc27711e86] Server Error Called by client'. Affects skill update flow at `https://clawhub.ai/skills/publish?updateSlug=chess-with-claw`. Retried multiple times over 6+ hours, tested on multiple devices, different slugs — all fail identically.

source_issues.title: Clawhub new version uploading not working
source_issues.evidence: Clicking 'New version' on a published skill shows: 'Something went wrong [CONVEX Q(skills:checkSlugAvailability)] [Request ID: a4a9fab971ef3f91] Server Error Called by client'. Steps to reproduce: open published skill → click 'New version' → error screen instead of the version flow.

signals.topic: Skill search fails to recall non-first-token keywords — entire catalog portions undiscoverable
signals.summary: Search only matches the first token of a slug or display name as a string prefix. Keywords that are not the first token (e.g., 'yijian' in 'baidu-yijian-vision') return zero results. Additionally, visibility decays over time as other skills get updated, pushing older skills out of the recency window.
signals.review_reason: P1: While count=1, the bug is architecturally systemic — it affects every skill whose slug/name does not start with the user's search keyword, and additionally causes time-based visibility decay. This is a fundamental discoverability failure that makes large portions of the catalog invisible to users. Code-level analysis and a full fix patch are provided.

source_issues.title: [Search] Skill search underrecall: non-first-token keywords never match, visibility decays over time
source_issues.evidence: Deep technical analysis with code-level evidence: `directPrefixSkillMatches` runs 4 string-prefix queries that all require the search term to be a prefix of the slug/first-token. 'yijian' in 'baidu-yijian-vision' matches zero results because 'yijian' is not a prefix of 'baidu-yijian-vision'. Visibility decay: `lexicalFallbackSkills` only scans most-recently-updated N skills — as other skills update, a skill gets pushed out and disappears from results entirely. Full architectural fix with code patch provided.

signals.topic: memory-core memory_search blocks Node.js event loop for 60+ seconds
signals.summary: Event loop delay spikes to 62,746ms; memory_search runs 63+ seconds; Discord gateway closes websocket; 17 agents affected fleet-wide; agent frozen with no self-recovery, requires restart.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: event loop freeze for 60+ seconds renders the Discord gateway unresponsive and kills all agent sessions. No self-recovery without restart. High impact across 17 agents fleet-wide.

source_issues.title: memory-core: memory_search blocks event loop for 60+ seconds — Discord gateway closes, agents hang
source_issues.evidence: Event loop delay spikes to 62,746ms; memory_search runs 63+ seconds; Discord gateway closes websocket; 17 agents affected fleet-wide; agent frozen, no self-recovery, requires restart

signals.topic: Context overflow recovery waits full ~900s auto-compaction timeout before fast tool-result truncation
signals.summary: User waited ~15 minutes for overflow recovery when truncation could have resolved it in milliseconds. Referenced by multiple prior issues in the compaction theme.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: user waited ~15 minutes for overflow recovery when truncation could have resolved it in milliseconds. Deterministic and reproducible when context overflow is tool-result driven. Referenced by multiple prior issues in the compaction theme.

Cross-platform (macOS confirmed), affects users with detailed custom instructions.

signals.topic: Refactor broke Image/Index node retrieval when no persistent document store is used, causing queries to fail
signals.summary: A refactor in PR #19382 (version 0.12.49) removed a document_exists check, causing Image/Index nodes to always require a persistent document store. Users who store all node metadata in the vector store without a separate document store now get ValueError on every query that returns Image/Index nodes.

signals.topic: Node serialization: model_dump() replacement broke IndexNode obj field deserialization, corrupting BM25 retriever data
signals.summary: PR #18447 replaced node.dict() with node.model_dump() throughout the codebase. The old .dict() was subclassed for IndexNode to wrap the obj field with __type__ using doc_to_json(). model_dump() is not subclassed, so deserialization via metadata_dict_to_node() fails and silently replaces the obj with a plain TextNode. Breaks BM25 retriever when IndexNodes are used.
aliases: model_dump vs dict subclassing for obj field
signals.review_reason: Data corruption bug: IndexNode objects are silently converted to plain TextNodes on retrieval through BM25 retriever. The failure is silent (no exception raised to user) and results in lost structured data, making this a 关键功能不可用 and 数据损坏 issue affecting anyone using IndexNodes with vector retrieval.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: obj serialization mismatch

BM25 retriever corpus deserialization is broken for IndexNodes.

signals.topic: Rate limiter async_acquire() uses threading.Lock, blocking the asyncio event loop and causing throughput collapse
signals.summary: TokenBucketRateLimiter and SlidingWindowRateLimiter use threading.Lock inside async methods. threading.Lock.acquire() is a blocking OS syscall that freezes all other coroutines for its duration. At 500 concurrent async_acquire() calls, the event loop is blocked for 200-340ms at a time, causing catastrophic latency spikes and throughput collapse in async LLM/embedding pipelines.
aliases: async rate limiter blocking other coroutines
signals.review_reason: 性能崩溃 in production async pipelines. threading.Lock inside async context is a fundamental concurrency anti-pattern that freezes the entire event loop, affecting all concurrent operations — not just the rate limiter itself. At high concurrency, this renders the entire async pipeline unresponsive.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: async_acquire() in TokenBucketRateLimiter and SlidingWindowRateLimiter blocks the asyncio event loop (threading.Lock used in async context)
source_issues.evidence: threading.Lock used inside async methods blocks the asyncio event loop thread during contention. With 500 concurrent async_acquire() calls, heartbeat coroutine detects event loop blocked 200-340ms at a time. Throughput collapse in any async LLM/embedding pipeline using rate_limiter. Reproducer provided.

signals.topic: Process group race condition: task completes before subprocess writes declared outputs, causing dependent tasks to fail
signals.summary: When a task spawns a subprocess that detaches or changes process group (via detached:true, setsid, or double-fork), Turbo prematurely signals task complete based on process group exit, but outputs haven't been written yet. Dependent tasks (^build style) then fail with 'Could not resolve' / 'Cannot find module' because files are not on disk. Observed in real CI at ~1.2% rate on Linux CI; synthetic modes reproduce at 99-100%.
aliases: premature task completion before outputs written
bunx detached process output not ready
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed race condition in Turbo's process group tracking that causes the primary build pipeline to fail non-deterministically. Dependent tasks fail with 'Could not resolve' errors and build artifacts are missing because the parent task was incorrectly marked complete before outputs were written. Real-world impact in CI pipelines at ~1.2% failure rate; synthetic reproduction at 99-100%. This is a main workflow blocker affecting the build pipeline.

source_issues.title: Task signaled complete before subprocess writes declared outputs when descendants leave the tracked process group
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction repo demonstrates 99.5-100% failure rate in detached/double-fork modes; real-world bunx --bun <cli> patterns fail at ~1.2% on Linux CI. Dependent tasks fail with 'Could not resolve' and Turbo prints 'WARNING no output files found for task'. Also affects Docker build pipelines where outputs aren't ready when dependents start.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker fails with literal workspace entries in package.json, breaking Docker builds
signals.summary: When package.json contains literal workspace entries (not globs) alongside Bun catalogs, turbo prune --docker generates an invalid pruned workspace package.json that references workspace names that no longer exist in the pruned output. Docker builds then fail with 'Workspace not found' errors.
aliases: turbo prune literal workspaces bun catalogs
docker build turbo prune bun catalogs
signals.review_reason: This bug breaks the critical Docker build pipeline use case of turbo prune. The pruned workspace becomes invalid and subsequent 'bun install' fails with 'Workspace not found' errors. This is a main workflow blocker for monorepo users using Docker + Bun with literal workspace configurations.

source_issues.title: literal workspaces + `turbo prune --docker` + `bun install` fails
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction repo demonstrates that 'bun install' fails in the pruned Docker image with 'error: Workspace not found scripts' and 'error: Workspace not found web-e2e-tests'. Breaking the Docker build pipeline. Also impacts users of Bun catalogs feature.

signals.topic: turbo prune emits invalid Bun lockfile for pruned workspaces with nested npm package entries, causing frozen lockfile Docker builds to fail
signals.summary: When turbo prune --docker generates a pruned Bun lockfile, it can drop necessary nested @npmcli/* package entries while keeping packages that depend on them. This causes 'bun install --frozen-lockfile' to fail in the Docker build stage with 'Failed to resolve prod dependency' and 'InvalidPackageInfo: failed to parse lockfile'.
signals.review_reason: This bug causes turbo prune to generate structurally invalid Bun lockfiles that cannot pass frozen lockfile validation in Docker builds. The pruned lockfile is missing dependency entries that are required by packages it retains, causing the Docker build to fail at the install stage. This is a main workflow blocker for CI/CD pipelines using Docker + Bun with frozen lockfiles.

source_issues.title: Turbo prune emits invalid Bun lockfile for pruned workspace with nested npm package entries
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction repo with Docker build demonstrates 'error: Failed to resolve prod dependency @npmcli/metavuln-calculator for package npm/@npmcli/arborist' and 'InvalidPackageInfo: failed to parse lockfile'. Docker build fails at 'RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts'.

signals.topic: SIGINT signal not forwarded to child processes when script-shell=sh, breaking graceful shutdown on Windows
signals.summary: When Turbo runs tasks with script-shell=sh (the Windows default set by npm), SIGINT signals from Ctrl+C are not forwarded to child processes. Node.js graceful shutdown sequences never trigger. On Windows, users cannot switch to bash due to security policy restrictions, leaving no workaround.
aliases: SIGINT not forwarded sh shell windows
graceful shutdown fails windows script-shell sh
signals.review_reason: This bug breaks the graceful shutdown workflow on Windows, which is the default platform for many developers. When pressing Ctrl+C, child processes never receive SIGINT and cannot perform cleanup (database connections, in-flight requests, temp file removal). This is a significant quality-of-life regression for Windows users in development and dev server scenarios.

source_issues.title: `SIGINT` is not forwarded properly when `script-shell=sh`
source_issues.evidence: Demonstrated with reproduction repo comparing bash vs sh behavior: with bash the graceful shutdown sequence fires and completes; with sh (Windows default) the process exits immediately without triggering graceful shutdown. Windows users cannot switch to bash due to security policy restrictions, leaving them with no workaround.

signals.topic: Services-mode + middleware.ts 导致部署在 'Deploying outputs' 阶段静默失败

signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（每次带 middleware.ts 的 services-mode 部署必败），有确定性最小复现，有根因定位，用户只能通过规避方案（放弃 services-mode 或删除 middleware.ts）绕过，直接阻断 experimentalServices 特性在 Next.js 项目中的使用。

source_issues.title: Services-Mode: Middleware routes are not exempted from scopeRoutesToServiceOwnership, breaking deploy outputs
source_issues.evidence: 完整5文件最小复现仓库，隔离矩阵证明 middleware.ts 是充分必要触发条件；删除则部署成功，恢复立即复现；Vercel 内部支持单据两个；社区多条相关线程印证同周 middleware 相关部署故障

source_issues.title: Agent thread fails to load after dev container rebuild (RemoteConnectionIdentity keyed on ephemeral container_id)

signals.topic: Agent edit_file tool in create mode fails with hard error when parent directories don't exist

Users must manually call create_directory first, which the agent doesn't do automatically.
aliases: edit_file create mode parent dir error
signals.review_reason: Agent 是 Zed 的核心卖点功能。edit_file 在 create 模式下无法创建新目录是高频场景的阻断 bug（创建新项目结构时几乎必然遇到），且用户被迫手动干预 agent 工作流，核心体验显著下降。

source_issues.title: agent: edit_file (create mode) should auto-create missing parent directories instead of erroring

Agent calls edit_file with mode: create and gets 'Can't create file: parent directory doesn't exist'. create_directory tool exists and supports mkdir -p semantics but edit_file doesn't invoke it. Workaround requires manually invoking create_directory first.
